confirmed.title: Every space switch routes spaceIDReassigned, migrating/destroying GridState
confirmed.mechanism: WorkspaceObserver.spaceChanged (WorkspaceObserver.swift:132-142) routes focusChanged(trigger:.spaceSwitched) -> StateManager.handle case .focusChanged (StateManager.swift:231-233) calls handleSpaceChanged() -> StateManager.swift:1744-1751 detects ANY display whose currentSpaceID changed (true for every normal desktop switch, not just macOS space-ID reassignment) and at StateManager.swift:1762-1769 routes .spaceIDReassigned(old,new) -> GridReconciler.handle (GridReconciler.swift:432-439, processed even during suppression) -> handleSpaceIDReassigned (GridReconciler.swift:914-944) -> GridState.migrateSpace (GridState.swift:207-233) which moves the old space's entire grid state (layout, cells, window assignments, focus) onto the new space ID, OVERWRITING spaces[newSpaceID] (GridState.swift:221) and DELETING spaces[oldSpaceID] (GridState.swift:222). The only guards (GridState.swift:208-212) are old!=new and old-has-significant-state; nothing checks whether the old space still exists in the OS (i.e. whether this was a reassignment vs a plain switch). For a user with two persistent desktops A and B that each have layouts: switching A->B transplants A's grid onto B (B's layout and window assignments permanently lost) and erases A's grid. The current log only shows fullscreen-space round-trips (3->414->3) where the bounce-back accidentally restores state.
confirmed.symptom: After switching between two desktops that both have layouts, one desktop's tiling is gone ('no layout applied') and the other suddenly has the wrong layout/window assignments; focus commands target windows that live on the other space.
confirmed.fixDirection: Only route spaceIDReassigned when the old space ID no longer exists in the refreshed state.spaces (true reassignment); plain switches should route a dedicated spaceActivated event.
confirmed.evidence: StateManager.swift:1745-1749 'if let oldSpaceID = oldSpaceIDs[display.uuid], display.currentSpaceID != oldSpaceID { ... await EventRouter.shared.route(.spaceIDReassigned(...'  GridState.swift:220-222 'oldState.spaceId = newSpaceID; spaces[newSpaceID] = oldState; spaces.removeValue(forKey: oldSpaceID)'. Logs: 122/122 correlation — grep -c spc.changed = 122, grep -c state.space_migrated.live = 122, reconcile.space.reassign.noop = 0; e.g. {"ev":"state.space_migrated.live","data":{"new":"414","old":"3","windows":[5771,5930,438,60,817,8071]},"ts":1781130413} fired for a persistent space (3) whose ID was never reassigned.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop: WorkspaceObserver.swift:132-142 routes focusChanged(.spaceSwitched) on every activeSpaceDidChange; StateManager.swift:227-233 dispatches to handleSpaceChanged(); StateManager.swift:1744-1769 diffs per-display currentSpaceID (SLSManagedDisplayGetCurrentSpace at :426 = the display's currently VISIBLE space, which changes on every plain desktop switch) and routes .spaceIDReassigned for any change with no check that the old space ID vanished from state.spaces; Grid/GridReconciler.swift:432-439 processes it explicitly BEFORE the suppressReconciliation guard (:442), so no suppression breaks the chain; handleSpaceIDReassigned (:914-944) guards only gridState != nil; Grid/GridState.swift:207-233 migrateSpace guards only old!=new + hasSignificantState (:279-281, layout-or-cells — not OS existence), then :221 unconditionally overwrites spaces[newSpaceID] and :222 deletes spaces[oldSpaceID]. Hunted for refutations and found none: suppression is explicitly bypassed, actor isolation is irrelevant (sequential flow, not a race), diffAndRouteSpaceEvents (:1739) doesn't gate the route, nothing restores the deleted entry, and git log shows the file unchanged since 1cf354e — code matches every cited line (minor path nit: GridReconciler/GridState live under Grid/). Independently reproduced the log correlation: 122 spc.changed / 122 state.space_migrated.live / 122 reconcile.space.reassign / 0 noop; a full transition census shows persistent spaces 3 and 6 round-tripping with monotonically-increasing fullscreen space IDs (105..419) — spaces 3/6 persist across all events, proving the route fires for plain visible-space changes, not true reassignments. The destructive two-layouts-on-one-display scenario is extrapolated (not yet in logs, this user has one tiled space per display) but is mechanically certain: A->B overwrites B's grid with A's and B's state is permanently lost even after switching back.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: StateManager.swift:421-428 refreshDisplayCurrentSpaces uses SLSManagedDisplayGetCurrentSpace — currentSpaceID is the display's visible space, so the :1745-1746 diff is true for every ordinary desktop switch. GridReconciler.swift:430-439 comment 'Space ID reassignment must always be processed ... cannot wait for suppression to end' proves suppression cannot break the chain. GridState.swift:221 'spaces[newSpaceID] = oldState' overwrites the destination unconditionally even when the destination space has its own significant state. Log census: all 122 transitions are persistent space 3 (display FCEC43D7) or 6 (display 89ED320F) paired with one-shot ascending IDs 105,112,...,419 (fullscreen spaces); 3 and 6 recur throughout, i.e. their IDs were never reassigned, yet each transition logged state.space_migrated.live.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code path re-verified end-to-end. (1) StateManager.swift:1741-1769 (handleSpaceChanged): for any display whose currentSpaceID differs from the pre-refresh snapshot, it unconditionally routes .spaceIDReassigned(old,new) — there is no check that the old space ID vanished from state.spaces (i.e. no distinction between a true macOS ID reassignment and a plain desktop switch). (2) GridReconciler.swift:429-438: spaceIDReassigned is explicitly processed even during suppression ('must always be processed'). (3) GridReconciler.swift:914-944 handleSpaceIDReassigned -> GridState.swift migrateSpace (Grid/GridState.swift:205-233): guards are only oldID != newID and hasSignificantState(old); it then does spaces[newSpaceID] = oldState and spaces.removeValue(forKey: oldSpaceID) — unconditionally overwriting any existing state at newSpaceID and deleting old. So switching between two laid-out persistent desktops on one display would transplant A onto B and erase A, exactly as claimed. Log evidence supports the unconditional routing: 122 spc.changed events, 122 state.space_migrated.live, 0 reconcile.space.reassign.noop (the only no-op path is empty old state, never an existence check). However, a uniq tally of ALL old/new pairs across 152,773 log lines shows every single migration is persistent↔ephemeral: space 3 (display FCEC43D7) or space 6 (display 89ED320F) round-tripping with a monotonically increasing fullscreen-space ID (105→419), always bouncing back within seconds, restoring state. Zero migrations where both IDs are persistent (<100). The destructive manifestation has never fired in real usage — this user runs one laid-out persistent desktop per display, so the data-loss trigger (two laid-out desktops on the same display) does not exist in their workflow; all observed migrations are the benign/intended fullscreen case. Mechanism is real and demonstrated by code + the 122/122 unconditional-routing correlation, but the harmful variant is latent, arguing for a severity downgrade from critical (latent data-loss bug for multi-desktop users, not an active failure here).
evidenceVerdict.addedEvidence: Log pair tally (grep state.space_migrated.live | grep -oE '"new":"...","old":"..."' | sort | uniq -c): all 122 migrations are 3↔{349,359,379,384,389,414,419,...} on display FCEC43D7 or 6↔{105..409} on display 89ED320F; awk filter for both IDs <100 returns zero rows — no persistent-to-persistent migration ever logged. reconcile.space.reassign.noop count = 0, confirming the only guard that ever fires is hasSignificantState, never an old-space-still-exists check (none exists in code). GridReconciler.swift:429-431 comment confirms spaceIDReassigned bypasses suppression by design. Grid/GridState.swift:221-222 'spaces[newSpaceID] = oldState; spaces.removeValue(forKey: oldSpaceID)' overwrites newSpaceID state with no significance check on the destination. Note: finding's file paths are slightly off — GridState.swift and GridReconciler.swift live under grid-server/Sources/GridServer/Grid/.

confirmed.title: SIGPIPE on client-socket send kills entire server
confirmed.mechanism: SocketServer.sendMessage (SocketServer.swift:233-254) writes replies with a raw BSD send(socket, ptr, count, 0) (SocketServer.swift:240-242). The only socket option ever set is SO_REUSEADDR on the listening socket (:33-34); accepted client sockets never get SO_NOSIGPIPE, macOS has no MSG_NOSIGNAL, and SIGPIPE is never set to SIG_IGN. Instead, CrashReporter.install() registers SIGPIPE as a FATAL signal (CrashReporter.swift:78 installSignal(SIGPIPE)) whose handler calls Darwin._exit(128 &+ sig) (CrashReporter.swift:168). A client that closes its socket between request and reply (or while subscribed via EventBroadcaster.broadcast -> sendMessage, EventBroadcaster.swift:34-39) makes the server's send() raise SIGPIPE; the fatal handler terminates the whole window manager with exit 141. The 'if sent < 0 ... sock.err' branch at :244-248 never runs because the signal fires before send returns EPIPE. Latent — no srv.fatal SIGPIPE in the current 13MB log.
confirmed.symptom: Entire grid-server process dies (tiling, hotkeys, borders all gone until restart) the moment any client disconnects between request and reply or mid-broadcast. Log shows srv.fatal SIGPIPE then srv.prev_exit on next start.
confirmed.fixDirection: Set SO_NOSIGPIPE on every accepted client socket (and/or signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN)), letting send() return EPIPE which the existing sock.err branch handles; drop SIGPIPE from CrashReporter's fatal-signal list.
confirmed.evidence: SocketServer.swift:240-242: 'let sent = data.withUnsafeBytes { ptr in send(socket, ptr.baseAddress, data.count, 0) }' — flags 0, no SO_NOSIGPIPE anywhere (only setsockopt SO_REUSEADDR at :34). CrashReporter.swift:78: 'installSignal(SIGPIPE)'; CrashReporter.swift:168: 'Darwin._exit(128 &+ sig)'. Repo-wide grep confirms no SIG_IGN/SO_NOSIGPIPE/MSG_NOSIGNAL.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop. (1) SocketServer.swift:240-242: sendMessage uses raw send(socket, ptr.baseAddress, data.count, 0) — flags 0; macOS lacks MSG_NOSIGNAL. (2) Read the entire file: the only setsockopt is SO_REUSEADDR on the listening socket (:33-34); accepted client sockets (:108-135) never get SO_NOSIGPIPE. (3) Repo-wide grep for SIG_IGN/NOSIGPIPE/MSG_NOSIGNAL: in grid-server main tree only SIGINT/SIGTERM are SIG_IGN'd (main.swift:114,118) — SIGPIPE is never ignored. (4) CrashReporter.swift:78 installs SIGPIPE as a fatal signal via sigaction; the handler (:122-169) writes srv.fatal and calls Darwin._exit(128 &+ sig) (:168) and never returns, so the 'sent < 0' branch at SocketServer.swift:244-248 is dead on this path. CrashReporter.install() is invoked at main.swift:79 before socketServer.start(). (5) Broadcast path confirmed: EventBroadcaster.swift:34-39 loops getClientSockets() and calls server.sendMessage; handleClient's defer (SocketServer.swift:141-151) closes the server-side fd asynchronously after client disconnect, leaving a real window where the fd is valid but the peer is closed. (6) Empirically verified the OS hop on this Darwin 25.2 host: a C test mirroring the server (sigaction handler with SA_RESETHAND, AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socketpair, peer closed, send flags 0) delivered signal 13 — output 'send returned -1 errno=32 got_signal=13'. With the server's non-returning handler, the process exits 141. (7) git log -- SocketServer.swift: last change 906deba, code unchanged vs cited lines. (8) ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json contains 0 srv.fatal lines, matching the 'latent' claim. No guard, actor isolation, or debounce breaks the mechanism; SA_RESETHAND only affects a second signal that never arrives.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: Empirical proof on the target host: /tmp/sigpipe_test.c (sigaction SIGPIPE handler with SA_RESETHAND, AF_UNIX socketpair, close peer, send(fd, buf, n, 0)) prints 'send returned -1 errno=32 got_signal=13 (SIGPIPE=13)' — confirming macOS raises SIGPIPE on UDS send-after-peer-close with flags 0. Also: CrashReporter.install() call site at main.swift:79 (before socketServer.start()), and main.swift:114/118 SIG_IGN covers only SIGINT/SIGTERM, proving SIGPIPE disposition is solely the fatal handler. Note: send does return EPIPE after a returning handler, but CrashReporter's handler _exits and never returns, so the EPIPE branch is unreachable — same conclusion as the finding with tighter wording.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code evidence actively demonstrates the mechanism. (1) Re-read /Users/r/repos/theGrid/grid-server/Sources/GridServer/CrashReporter.swift:73-78 — SIGPIPE is installed alongside SIGSEGV/SIGABRT etc. as a fatal signal; the async-signal-safe handler (:122-168) writes a srv.fatal JSONL line and calls Darwin._exit(128 &+ sig), i.e. exit 141 for SIGPIPE. main.swift:318 even includes a deliberate `case "SIGPIPE": raise(SIGPIPE)` debug path confirming SIGPIPE is treated as process-fatal. (2) Re-read SocketServer.swift — accept loop (:101-137) sets no options on accepted client sockets; sendMessage (:233-254) uses raw `send(socket, ptr.baseAddress, data.count, 0)` at :240-242; the only setsockopt in the file is SO_REUSEADDR on the listener (:33-34). Repo-wide grep for SO_NOSIGPIPE/MSG_NOSIGNAL/SIG_IGN confirms SIGPIPE is never ignored anywhere in grid-server, so the existing `sent < 0` EPIPE branch (:244-248) is unreachable for a closed peer — the fatal handler fires first. EventBroadcaster.broadcast (EventBroadcaster.swift:34-39) iterates a socket snapshot and calls the same unprotected sendMessage, so a subscriber dying mid-broadcast would also kill the server. (3) Log evidence: grepped ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json (152,773 lines, ~10 days): zero srv.fatal, zero SIGPIPE, zero srv.prev_exit, zero sock.err — and critically, zero event.broadcast events plus 237 matched sock.connect/sock.disconnect pairs, meaning the trigger (client closing before reply, or broadcast to a dead subscriber) never occurs with the current synchronous request/reply clients and no event subscribers exist. The bug is real and code-proven but latent in practice, so severity should come down from critical.
evidenceVerdict.addedEvidence: main.swift:318 `case "SIGPIPE": raise(SIGPIPE)` — debug harness path proving SIGPIPE is intentionally wired into the fatal-signal handler. Log absence evidence: 152,773 lines spanning ts 1780352807-1781204867 contain 0 srv.fatal, 0 srv.prev_exit, 0 srv.atexit, 0 sock.err, 0 event.broadcast, and 237 clean sock.connect/sock.disconnect pairs — the EventBroadcaster path (the most plausible SIGPIPE trigger) has never executed in the logged window, and no client has ever closed its socket early enough to make send() fail.

confirmed.title: GridReconciler is an unsynchronized plain class — suppressionDepth/fencedWindows/pendingLaunchTarget mutated from 4+ concurrent contexts; 7x duplicate sweep processing observed
confirmed.mechanism: GridReconciler.swift:21 declares 'class GridReconciler: StateEventHandler' (not an actor; Package.swift is swift-tools 5.9, no strict concurrency, so data races compile silently). Its handle() (:414) is a nonisolated async method, so when the EventRouter actor awaits it (EventRouter.swift:205) it runs on the global concurrent executor. Mutable fields are touched from: (1) EventRouter dispatch tasks — handle() reads suppressReconciliation (:442) and mutates fencedWindows via isWindowFenced lazy expiry (:230-243) and pendingLaunchTarget consume (:799); (2) the 300ms sweep timer's detached Tasks on a utility queue (:325-331 'Task { await self.focusSweep(); await self.rejectedWindowSweep() }') with no overlap guard; (3) concurrent socket command threads — every command runs executeAction's non-atomic 'suppressionDepth += 1' / '-= 1' (:99, :106, :119) plus acquireFence/releaseFence (:163-186) from GridWindowMove.swift:255/343 (SocketServer clientQueue is concurrent, SocketServer.swift:10); (4) the main queue — PickerManager.swift:238 'DispatchQueue.main.async { reconcilerRef?.updatePendingLaunchTargetPID(pid) }' (:197-201). Production proof of overlap: rejectedWindowSweep (:384-410) does check-then-act with awaits between; the log shows SEVEN identical sweep.unrejected + SEVEN reconcile.win.create entries for wid 5760 at the same second — impossible for a 300ms timer unless >=7 sweep tasks were in flight simultaneously. Duplicates were saved only by GridState.assignWindow's idempotency (GridState.swift:330-332). Latent escalation: a torn suppressionDepth decrement leaves suppressReconciliation permanently true (all create/destroy/focus events dropped until restart), and concurrent Dictionary mutation of fencedWindows is undefined behavior (crash-class).
confirmed.symptom: Duplicate window-create processing (redundant layout applies / border-sync storms with visible flicker) when a rejected window matures; latent risk of permanent reconciliation freeze (new windows never tile, borders stop following focus) or an EXC_BAD_ACCESS crash in dictionary access.
confirmed.fixDirection: Convert GridReconciler to an actor (or confine it to a serial executor) — all callers already await its methods — and make the sweep timer skip ticks while a sweep task is still running.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:21 'class GridReconciler: StateEventHandler'; :57 'private var suppressionDepth: Int = 0'; :63 'private var fencedWindows: [UInt32: CFAbsoluteTime] = [:]'; :99 'suppressionDepth += 1'; :327-330 timer-spawned Tasks; PickerManager.swift:238 main-queue write; SocketServer.swift:10 concurrent client queue; Package.swift:1 '// swift-tools-version: 5.9'. Logs: {"ev":"sweep.unrejected","data":{"h":950,"w":452,"wid":5760},"ts":1780806182} x7 followed by {"ev":"reconcile.win.create","data":{"cell":"left","wid":5760},"ts":1780806182} x7; same pattern x3 for wid 5735 at ts 1780805427.

codeVerdict.reasoning: I set out to refute this and could not — every hop re-traced in code and the log evidence independently re-verified. (1) Structure: /Users/r/repos/theGrid/grid-server/Sources/GridServer/Grid/GridReconciler.swift:21 is 'class GridReconciler: StateEventHandler' (plain class, no actor, no locks anywhere in the file); mutable fields suppressionDepth (:57), fencedWindows (:63), pendingLaunchTarget (:49) exactly as claimed. Non-atomic 'suppressionDepth += 1' at :99 and 'max(0, suppressionDepth - 1)' at :106/:119; beginAction/endAction also mutate it (:135, :146). Package.swift:1 is swift-tools-version 5.9 and grep found zero StrictConcurrency/swiftSettings flags, so these races compile silently. (2) Concurrency hops: handle() (:414) is a nonisolated async method on a non-Sendable class, so when EventRouter (an actor) awaits it in route() (EventRouter.swift ~:205, 'try await handler.handle(event, context:)') it runs on the multi-threaded global concurrent executor — no serialization. The sweep timer (:317-335) fires on its own dispatch queue and spawns unstructured 'Task { await self.focusSweep(); await self.rejectedWindowSweep() }' (:327-330) with NO overlap guard — I looked specifically for an in-flight flag or task handle and there is none. SocketServer.swift:10 confirms 'clientQueue = DispatchQueue(..., attributes: .concurrent)'. GridWindowMove.swift:~256 calls gridReconciler.acquireFence and :~343 releaseFence (synchronous dictionary mutation of fencedWindows). Picker/PickerManager.swift:239 (finding said 238, off by one) is 'DispatchQueue.main.async { reconcilerRef?.updatePendingLaunchTargetPID(pid) }' — a main-thread write to pendingLaunchTarget (:197-201) racing the global-executor reads at :404/:424 and the writes at :793/:799. (3) Check-then-act: rejectedWindowSweep (:384-410) does getRejectedWindows → await getState → unrejectWindow → handleWindowCreated with suspension points between check and act. (4) Log proof re-verified directly: ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json contains exactly 7 '"ev":"sweep.unrejected"' entries for wid 5760 all at ts 1780806182, followed by 7 reconcile.win.create at the same ts. I tested the only sequential alternative — re-reject/unreject cycles per tick — and it fails twice over: GridState.swift:451-453 shows unrejectWindow removes the wid from the actor-isolated set, GridState.swift:84 confirms GridState is an actor, there are zero re-reject log entries between the 7 (the only bail is 4s earlier at ts ...178), and a 300ms timer with 50ms leeway yields at most ~4 ticks per second, not 7. Also the 7-grouped-then-7-grouped ordering (all unrejected before any create) is the signature of >=7 tasks suspended in flight together, not alternating sequential pairs. (5) Idempotency rescue confirmed: GridState.swift:326-329 'if cell.windows.contains(windowID) { return }'. (6) git log shows the file last changed in 713cf7a, already in HEAD — code unchanged since the finding; every cited line matched what I read. The only hop I could not verify end-to-end is whether socket commands run executeAction concurrently in practice (MessageHandler implementation chain not fully traced), but that is one of four contexts and the timer/EventRouter/main-queue contexts plus the 7x log overlap prove the mechanism independently of it.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: GridState.swift:451-453 'func unrejectWindow(_ windowID: UInt32) { rejectedWindows.remove(windowID) }' on 'actor GridState' (:84) — eliminates the sequential re-processing alternative: once any sweep unrejects wid 5760 it cannot reappear without an explicit rejectWindow call, and the log shows none between the 7 entries. Log ordering detail: all 7 sweep.unrejected entries precede all 7 reconcile.win.create entries at the identical second — the lockstep signature of >=7 concurrent sweep tasks all having passed getRejectedWindows before any completed handleWindowCreated (handleWindowCreated does slow AX layout work, giving the overlap window). Log file contains 16 total sweep.unrejected events. GridReconciler.swift:135/:146 — beginAction/endAction are additional non-atomic suppressionDepth mutation sites beyond the three cited, callable from nudge-mode keystrokes. endAction (:153-157) spawns yet another unstructured Task touching shared state.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Re-read GridReconciler.swift and grepped the production log. Code: :21 plain 'class GridReconciler: StateEventHandler' (not actor), Package.swift:1 swift-tools 5.9 (data races compile silently); :57/:63 mutable suppressionDepth/fencedWindows; :99/:106/:119 non-atomic depth mutation inside executeAction; :317-335 the 300ms timer's setEventHandler spawns an unstructured 'Task { await focusSweep(); await rejectedWindowSweep() }' per tick with no overlap guard; :384-410 rejectedWindowSweep is check-then-act with suspension points (await getRejectedWindows at :388, await getState at :391) before unrejectWindow at :397 — concurrent sweep tasks all pass the check before any removes the wid. Log: grep '"ev":"sweep.unrejected"' shows exactly the claimed pattern — 7 identical entries for wid 5760 at ts 1780806182 and 3 for wid 5735 at ts 1780805427, each matched by 7x/3x 'reconcile.win.create' for the same wid/ts, plus 8x duplicated bdr.refresh/bdr.assignments downstream. evidenceVerdict.addedEvidence: Logger-artifact rule-out at ts 1780806182: 'grep "ts":1780806182 | sort | uniq -c' shows 7x sweep.unrejected(wid 5760), 7x reconcile.win.create(wid 5760), 8x bdr.refresh{"cell":"left","count":1}, 8x bdr.assignments — while win.destroyed(5735), ev.win.destroy(5735), reconcile.win.destroy(5735), sweep.correct(osWid 5760), bdr.retarget, bdr.rebuild each appear exactly once. confirmed.title: windowCreated/windowDestroyed events silently dropped during suppression are never replayed — window permanently untiled, dead windows linger up to 30s
confirmed.mechanism: Every user command runs inside GridReconciler.executeAction (GridReconciler.swift:91-129), which increments suppressionDepth; beginAction/endAction sessions last arbitrarily long — nudge mode holds suppression across keystrokes (GridCommandRouter.swift:790-861) and picker.result holds one across the picker flow (PickerManager.swift:198-272; 64x action.begin label picker.result in logs). While suppressed, handle() silently drops all non-focus, non-pending events at GridReconciler.swift:441-444 ('// Skip other events when suppressed / if suppressReconciliation { return }') — including .windowCreated, .windowDestroyed, .windowMinimized, .windowMoved — with no deferred queue or replay. A dropped .windowCreated is unrecoverable: StateManager (registered with EventRouter FIRST, main.swift:161 vs :166) already ingested the window into state.windows (StateManager.swift:1503), so the 3s poll's dedupe never re-emits the create (StateManager.swift:1272-1286 only routes windowCreated for windows NOT in state); the window was never rejected, so rejectedWindowSweep (:388-393) and handleWindowMoved's unreject path (:1025 'guard ... isWindowRejected') skip it; focusSweep returns early for untracked windows (:348); StateValidator only prunes, never adopts (StateValidator.swift:170-196); sweepDisplacedWindows iterates only windows already tracked in GridState (:1394) and skips wids missing from wmState (:1410-1413). A dropped .windowDestroyed symmetrically leaves a dead wid splitting its cell until StateValidator's ~30s pruneDeadWindows pass (StateValidator.swift:202-224). Log analysis confirms drops occur: 15 of 944 created wids never produced any reconcile.win.create*/sweep event, 14 of those 15 arrived while an action was open.
confirmed.symptom: A window opened while a hotkey command, layout apply, nudge session, or the picker is in flight permanently floats untiled — no border, invisible to focus navigation — until the layout is manually reapplied. A window closed during suppression leaves a ghost split / dead-window border in its cell for up to 30s.
confirmed.fixDirection: Queue (don't drop) windowCreated/windowDestroyed events received during suppression and replay them when suppressionDepth returns to 0; alternatively have the depth-0 sweep also scan for tileable windows absent from every GridState cell and remove tracked wids absent from wmState.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:441-444 verified in source: '// Skip other events when suppressed\n if suppressReconciliation { return }' (silent, no log). StateManager.swift:1272-1286 poll dedupe '// Track for windowCreated event routing (only if actually added)'. Logs: 1957 hits of reconcile.focus.suppressed showing how often events land during suppression; 11 hits of {"ev":"validate.win.prune","data":{"reason":"dead","wid":8457}} (the 30s backstop firing); 15/944 created wids with no reconciler reaction, e.g. wids 7819-7827 (Ghostty, ts 1781067035) and 6200/6202 (Chrome, ts 1780882353) all during an open action.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop in source. Drop site verified: GridReconciler.swift:441-444 returns silently while suppressed for all events except focusChanged (:416), pendingLaunchTarget windowCreated (:421-428), and spaceIDReassigned (:432) — windowCreated/windowDestroyed/windowMoved/windowMinimized are all dropped with no queue or replay. Suppression sessions verified: executeAction (GridReconciler.swift:91-129), nudge beginAction/endAction (GridCommandRouter.swift:790/826/861), picker.result (PickerManager.swift:198). No-replay verified: EventRouter.swift:202-205 dispatches sequentially to all handlers, StateManager.handle ingests windowCreated unconditionally into state.windows (StateManager.swift:203→1503, no suppression gate), and the 3s poll routes windowCreated only for windows NOT already in state (StateManager.swift:1272-1286), so the create event is never re-emitted. All claimed dead-end recovery paths verified: focusSweep early-returns for untracked windows (:348); rejectedWindowSweep iterates only the rejected list (:388-393) and a dropped create was never rejected; handleWindowMoved requires isWindowRejected (:1025); handleFocusChanged only sets focus if the window already has a cell (:878-883); sweepDisplacedWindows iterates only tracked wids (:1401) and skips wids absent from wmState (:1410-1412); StateValidator.validate runs only prune passes (StateValidator.swift:178-181), never adopts. confirmed.title: focusSweep reverts focus mid-command: never consults the fence, move commands run unsuppressed, and the suppression check is TOCTOU
confirmed.mechanism: Three gaps in one path. (1) No fence check: the 300ms focusSweep (GridReconciler.swift:41 sweepInterval=0.3, started :317-335) compares StateManager's cached OS focus against GridState focus (:344-352) and corrects GridState + borders on mismatch (:360-371), but never consults fencedWindows — the fence (:63, :827-839) only guards handleFocusChanged. (2) Moves unsuppressed: GridCommandRouter.swift:183-184 'case "window": return try await handleWindow(parsed)' has no executeAction wrapper (unlike 'case "focus"' at :176), so while moveWindowToCell runs — GridState focus set at GridWindowMove.swift:261, slow AX placements :322, AX focus :331 — the sweep can fire mid-flight, read the not-yet-updated wmState.metadata.focusedWindowID (:345), and setFocus back to the OLD window (:360), repainting borders to it (:367-371). The subsequent real OS focus event for the moved window is then DROPPED because that window is fenced (:827-830), so GridState keeps the wrong focus until the next sweep cycle. (3) TOCTOU: even for suppressed commands, the sweep checks 'guard !suppressReconciliation' exactly once at :341, then suspends across six awaits (getState :344, findSpaceContaining :348, getFocusedWindow :351, getWindowCell :355, getCellWindows :358) before writing at :360 — an executeAction beginning after the check (suppressionDepth += 1 at :99) does not stop the sweep's stale write; the reverse interleaving (sweep reads stale focusedWindowID=A right after an action focused B) also holds. StateManager only updates metadata.focusedWindowID after the AX focus event lands, widening the stale window.
confirmed.symptom: Focused border flicks/ping-pongs back to the previously focused window ~0-300ms after a focus or move command; with rapid sequential moves, a follow-up command reads the reverted focusedCell and moves/focuses the wrong window; sweep.correct entries adjacent to action.start/end pairs.
confirmed.fixDirection: Have focusSweep skip windows present in fencedWindows (both osWindowID and the grid-focused wid), wrap 'window' commands in executeAction, and re-check suppression (or a generation counter incremented by beginAction) immediately before the setFocus/updateFocus writes.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:339-360: 'private func focusSweep() async { guard !suppressReconciliation else { return } ... let gridFocusedWID = await gridState.getFocusedWindow(spaceID: spaceID); guard gridFocusedWID != osWindowID else { return } ... await gridState.setFocus(...)' — no isWindowFenced call anywhere in the function, six awaits between guard and write. GridCommandRouter.swift:183 'case "window": return try await handleWindow(parsed)' (no executeAction). Logs: 51 occurrences of sweep.correct, e.g. {"ev":"sweep.correct","data":{"cell":"left","gridWid":117,"osWid":6439,"space":"6"},"ts":1781189865}.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop in code. (1) GridReconciler.swift:339-379 focusSweep contains no isWindowFenced/isCellMateOfFencedWindow call — fence checks exist only in handleFocusChanged (:827-830, :836-839), exactly as claimed. (2) GridCommandRouter.swift:183-184 routes "window" commands without executeAction (focus at :176 is wrapped); grep of GridWindowMove.swift confirms zero executeAction/suppression usage — moves rely solely on fencing (acquireFence :255/:428, releaseFence :343/:513), which the sweep ignores. (3) GridWindowMove.swift:261 sets GridState focus, :322 applies slow AX placements, :331 issues AX focus; the sweep reads StateManager's cached focusedWindowID (:344-345), which only updates when the AX focus event lands (StateManager.swift:755/:802), so mid-move it reads the OLD window, mismatches at :352, and reverts GridState at :360 + borders :367-371. The real OS focus event for the moved window is then dropped by the fence at :827-830, leaving GridState wrong until the next 300ms tick. (4) TOCTOU: guard !suppressReconciliation checked once at :341, six awaits (:344,:348,:351,:355,:358) before the write at :360, no re-check; executeAction's suppressionDepth+=1 at :99 cannot stop a sweep already past the guard. Refutation hunt failed: GridReconciler is a plain class (line 21), not an actor; Package.swift is swift-tools-version 5.9 with no swiftSettings/defaultIsolation/StrictConcurrency, so nothing serializes the sweep (Task on global executor, :327) against commands — even suppressionDepth is an unsynchronized var, making the race surface wider than claimed. No debounce: timer fires unconditionally every 300ms (:317-335). git log shows no fix since 713cf7a. Caveat: in log sampling I found no sweep.correct strictly inside a fence.acquire/release window (fences held sub-second), so the in-move hit is a narrow probabilistic window in practice, but 51 sweep.correct entries confirm the sweep actively rewrites focus in production and the post-action stale-read interleaving (focus command ends, StateManager cache still stale, sweep reverts) needs no fence at all.

GridWindowMove.swift:255 acquireFence before any mutation and :343 releaseFence after border sync confirm the fence brackets exactly the window the sweep can corrupt; the move's own border sync at :340 paints from the sweep-reverted GridState, so the wrong border persists past the move. Log: fence.acquire/release pairs are sub-second (e.g. lines 691/714, 50908/50917 same ts), bounding how often the 300ms sweep lands mid-move; 51 sweep.correct entries total, with same-second win.focus+sweep.correct pairs at log lines 16499/16526 showing the sweep actively rewriting focus during transitions.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code claims verified: GridReconciler.swift:339-379 focusSweep has no isWindowFenced call and exactly one suppression guard (:341) before 5 awaits and the setFocus write (:360); GridCommandRouter.swift:183-184 routes 'window' without executeAction (vs 'focus' at :176); the move path uses fences only (GridWindowMove.swift:255/343, 428/513 acquireFence/releaseFence) with no suppression — so the latent race exists structurally. But the LOG evidence actively contradicts the claimed harmful manifestation: (a) grep of ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json (152,773 lines) shows 96 'fence.acquire' events yet ZERO 'sweep.correct' inside any fence window and none adjacent to window-move commands; (b) the cascade step 'real OS focus event for the moved window is then DROPPED because fenced' (GridReconciler.swift:828 reconcile.focus.fenced) has ZERO occurrences in the entire log — that code path has never fired; (c) the 51 'sweep.correct' hits cited as evidence are misattributed — every examined instance corrects GridState TOWARD the genuinely OS-focused window, not away from it: log line 144447 (right after action.end focus.right) is preceded by 'focus.mismatch.accept actual:8071 requested:60', i.e. the command's target failed to take focus and the sweep matched the real OS focus; line 141636 follows a new Chrome window (8319) winning focus before GridState tracked it; lines 126713/127029/136879 follow organic appActivated focus changes; 128368/143706 follow layout.apply where focus events were intentionally suppressed (reconcile.focus.suppressed) and the sweep is the designed recovery path. Verdict is 'suspected' not 'refuted' because the code-level race window is real and timing-dependent (could fire under loads not represented in this log), but no log entry demonstrates the mechanism, and the finding's own log evidence turns out to show the sweep working as designed. Severity downgrade: zero harmful occurrences across 152k lines including rapid sequential focus.right commands (3 dispatches within 1s at ts 1781152451-1452) and 96 fenced moves means 'high' overstates real-world impact; this is a latent hardening issue, not an active defect.

confirmed.title: Fence is not refcounted — overlapping moves of the same window strip each other's fence
confirmed.mechanism: Commands are fully concurrent: each CLI/hotkey invocation is a separate socket connection handled on a concurrent queue (SocketServer.swift:10 'clientQueue = DispatchQueue(label: "com.thegrid.client", attributes: .concurrent)'), and GridCommandRouter.dispatch is invoked per-request with no serialization. A same-space move acquires a per-window fence (GridWindowMove.swift:255 acquireFence) -> mutates GridState (:258-261) -> applies AX placements (:322) -> AX-focuses the window (:331) -> syncs borders (:340) -> releases the fence (:343). acquireFence just overwrites the expiry (GridReconciler.swift:168-171 'fencedWindows[windowID] = expiresAt'), and releaseFence unconditionally deletes the entry (:179-182 'fencedWindows.removeValue(forKey:)') — verified in source, no nesting count. When the user holds the move hotkey, move B starts before move A finishes: A-acquire, B-acquire (overwrite), A-release (entry deleted), B still mid-flight unfenced. Late/stale OS focus events for that window now pass the fence check in handleFocusChanged (:827-830) and overwrite the focus move B just set (:878-892), reverting focus/borders. This is a logic defect independent of the missing class-level synchronization: it reproduces even with fully serialized access. Production log shows the exact interleaving (two fence.acquire for wid 60 before any release at ts 1781156600).
confirmed.symptom: During rapid repeated window moves (held hotkey), focus and the focused border ping-pong between the moved window and the previously focused window; occasionally the next move grabs the wrong window because GridState focus was reverted mid-sequence.
confirmed.fixDirection: Make fencedWindows a refcount (or per-acquisition token) so releaseFence only removes the entry when the count reaches zero; alternatively serialize move commands per window.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:170 'fencedWindows[windowID] = expiresAt' / :181 'fencedWindows.removeValue(forKey: windowID)' (verified, no nesting count). SocketServer.swift:10 concurrent client queue. Log (thegrid-server.json): {"ev":"fence.acquire","data":{"reason":"move.same","wids":[60]},"ts":1781156600} {"ev":"fence.acquire",..."wids":[60]},"ts":1781156600} {"ev":"fence.release","data":{"wids":[60]},"ts":1781156600} {"ev":"fence.release",..."ts":1781156600} — second acquire before first release.
confirmed.logSignature: "ev":"fence.acquire" appearing twice for the same wid with no intervening "ev":"fence.release" (same-second duplicates)

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop in current HEAD. (1) Concurrency: SocketServer.swift:10 concurrent clientQueue + :133 per-client dispatch; MessageHandler.swift:52 spawns an unstructured Task per request and dispatchAndRespond (MessageHandler.swift:1389) spawns another; GridCommandRouter is a plain class (GridCommandRouter.swift:32) and handleWindow (:489) calls gridWindowMove.moveWindow with NO executeAction/suppression wrapper (contrast: focus domain at :175 IS wrapped). (2) Move flow: GridWindowMove.swift:255 acquireFence -> :257-260 GridState mutation -> AX apply (~:322) -> focusWindowByID (~:331) -> border sync (~:340) -> releaseFence :343, exactly as claimed. (3) No refcount: GridReconciler.swift:170 'fencedWindows[windowID] = expiresAt' is a plain dictionary overwrite; :181 releaseFence does unconditional removeValue; GridReconciler is 'class GridReconciler: StateEventHandler' (:21) with no @MainActor and no lock — no actor isolation serializes the overlap, and the adjacent suppressionDepth (:57) IS refcounted, confirming the asymmetry. (4) Consequence: handleFocusChanged's direct fence check (:827-830) AND the cell-mate guard (:836-840) both key off the fencedWindows entry; once A's release strips B's fence, late OS focus events pass both guards and overwrite GridState focus (:881-886) and borders (:888-894). The code comment at :832-835 explicitly names the collateral event ('previously-focused co-cell window surfacing briefly') that the stripped fence now admits. (5) Code unchanged since finding: git log shows last touch 713cf7a. (6) Log evidence independently verified in ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json: two consecutive fence.acquire {reason:move.same, wids:[60]} before two fence.release, all ts 1781156600 — overlapping same-window moves occur in production. Hunted for refutations (actor isolation, command serialization, semaphores, fence timeout semantics, suppression coverage of moves) and found none.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: GridCommandRouter.swift:175 — the 'focus' domain is wrapped in gridReconciler.executeAction (refcounted suppression) while the 'window' domain (:489) is not, so moves rely solely on the non-refcounted fence. MessageHandler.swift:52 and :1389 — two layers of per-request unstructured Task spawning, proving zero command serialization. GridReconciler.swift:836-840 — the cell-mate fence guard (isCellMateOfFencedWindow) is also defeated when the fence is stripped, which is the path that produces the previously-focused-window ping-pong symptom; its own comment documents the exact event class it exists to block. Log lines verified verbatim in ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json (acquire/acquire/release/release for wid 60 at ts 1781156600, file order = write order).

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Mechanism actively demonstrated in both code and logs. Code: GridReconciler.swift:170 acquire is a plain dictionary overwrite (fencedWindows[windowID] = expiresAt) and :181 release is an unconditional removeValue — no refcount/token; SocketServer.swift:10 confirms the concurrent client queue, and GridWindowMove.swift:255/:343 are the same-space acquire/release call sites. Logs: grepped ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json (152,790 lines, 192 fence events) and extracted the full event window at ts 1781156600 — two move commands for wid 60 dispatched same-second (cmd+ctrl-h then cmd+ctrl-l), fence.acquire twice before any fence.release, and move B's ax.focus/ev.win.move events occur AFTER the first fence.release, proving move B executed its AX-focus phase with the window unfenced (A's release stripped B's fence). Same-second acquire/release bursts for one wid recur throughout the log (wids 60, 8603), so the trigger is common during held-hotkey moves. However, absence evidence caps the impact: reconcile.focus.fenced (GridReconciler.swift:828, the event logged when the fence actually drops an OS focus event) appears 0 times in the entire log, as do reconcile.focus.fenced.cell and fence.expired — the fence has never blocked a focus event in ~10 days of production use, so the early strip has never demonstrably caused the claimed focus revert. Additionally, both overlapping moves AX-focus the same window, and handleFocusChanged (GridReconciler.swift:858-885) resolves the cell from current GridState at processing time, so a stale pass-through event for the moved window largely re-asserts the focus the second move already set. Defect is real; observed harm is not, hence downgrade from high.

Move B's AX mutation/focus ran after its fence was stripped by move A's release. confirmed.title: WindowManipulator sole-AX-window fallback is unguarded — manipulations land on the wrong window (residual gap after 1cf354e)
confirmed.mechanism: Commit 1cf354e added the shouldUseSoleWindowFallback guard ONLY to StateManager.getAXProperties (StateManager.swift:586-596 checks _AXUIElementGetWindow(windows[0], &soleWindowID) and refuses when the sole window resolves to a DIFFERENT CG ID than the queried phantom). WindowManipulator.getAXElement (WindowManipulator.swift:57-85) still has the original unguarded fallback: after failing the ID match loop, 'if windows.count == 1 { return windows[0] }' (:78-80, verified in source) with no resolution check and NO log (the ax.fail not_in_list at :82 only fires when count != 1). Every manipulation path funnels through getAXElement: setWindowFrame(context:) (:208-217), moveWindow (:160-191), resizeWindow (:194-205), focusWindowWithRaise's AXRaise (:477-479), MessageHandler window ops, and GridApply via the WindowController conformance (:578-581). When a phantom/rejected window ID of an app whose AX list shows exactly one window is targeted, the operation is silently applied to the app's one REAL window — moved/resized to the phantom's cell frame — while setWindowFrame(context:) at :213-214 writes that frame into state under the PHANTOM's windowID, so state disagrees with reality for both windows. This is a residual gap, not a restatement of the shipped fix: git show 1cf354e's WindowManipulator hunk only added isSizeSettable.
confirmed.symptom: A real window suddenly jumps/resizes to a cell it was never assigned to when the reconciler or layout-apply touches a phantom ID; focus raise lands on the wrong same-app window; state frame recorded for a phantom while the real window's state frame goes stale.
confirmed.fixDirection: Apply the same shouldUseSoleWindowFallback(resolved:soleWindowID:queriedID:) guard in WindowManipulator.getAXElement before returning windows[0], and log when the fallback fires.
confirmed.evidence: WindowManipulator.swift:76-80 verified in source: '// Fallback: If only one AX window exists, use it (handles apps like Ghostty where SkyLight reports multiple phantom window IDs but AX only sees one real window)\n if windows.count == 1 { return windows[0] }' — no _AXUIElementGetWindow check. Contrast StateManager.swift:586-596 (guarded). setWindowFrame(context:) :212-215 writes state for the queried ID after manipulating the wrong element.

(1) The unguarded fallback exists verbatim at WindowManipulator.swift:76-80: after the ID-match loop fails, `if windows.count == 1 { return windows[0] }` with no _AXUIElementGetWindow resolution check; the `ax.fail not_in_list` log at :82 only fires when count != 1, so the fallback is silent. (3) `git show 1cf354e -- WindowManipulator.swift` confirms that commit's only change to this file was adding isSizeSettable + the fixed-size skip; the fallback predates and survived the fix, so this is a residual gap, not a restatement. (4) Every manipulation path funnels through getAXElement as claimed: moveWindow :161, resizeWindow :195, setWindowFrame(context:) :209, focusWindowWithRaise AX raise :477-479, focusWindowFallback :493-495, moveWindowToDisplay :543, WindowController conformance :578-581 (GridApply/GridNudge), MessageHandler.swift:399/:423. confirmed.title: focusWindowByID verifies against stale cached focus (single Task.yield), causing spurious mismatch/retry and wrong 'actual' propagation
confirmed.mechanism: GridFocus.focusWindowByID calls windowController.focusWindow (GridFocus.swift:402) which is WindowManipulator's port conformance (WindowManipulator.swift:572-574) — it does NOT call stateManager.setFocusedWindow (only the unused context variant at WindowManipulator.swift:513-519 does). Verification then does a single 'await Task.yield()' (GridFocus.swift:414) and reads cached postState.metadata.focusedWindowID (:418-419). That cache is only updated when the OS focus notification travels AX-callback -> Task -> EventRouter actor -> StateManager.applyWindowFocus (StateManager.swift:754-758) — a main-runloop round trip that one yield essentially never covers. So 'actual' is frequently the PREVIOUSLY focused window: a spurious focus.mismatch fires (:421-427), a redundant second AX raise is issued (:452), and if still stale, the stale wid is returned as accepted reality (:458-464). Downstream: (a) cycleFocus (:261-284) treats a returned stale 'actual' outside the cell as 'window genuinely unfocusable, try next' (comment at :283) and issues focus calls for further windows even though the first focus succeeded — skipping windows; (b) moveFocus->focusCellByID ignores the returned actual entirely (:359) so GridState focus and the CLI return value can disagree with the OS until focusSweep corrects 300ms later.
confirmed.symptom: Doubled window raises on focus commands; cycle-focus occasionally jumping two windows or briefly raising several windows; CLI/borders momentarily highlighting a different window than the one actually focused.
confirmed.fixDirection: Have the WindowController port update StateManager focus synchronously on success (like the context variant), or verify via a direct AX focused-window query instead of the event-fed cache.
confirmed.evidence: GridFocus.swift:414 'await Task.yield()' with comment admitting 'without this yield, the verification read can fire before the notification lands and report the *previous* focused window'; WindowManipulator.swift:572-574 'func focusWindow(windowID:pid:) async -> Bool { return focusWindow(pid: pid, windowID: windowID) }' (no state write). Logs: 146 focus.mismatch, 12 focus.mismatch.accept; burst at ts 1780799211: ax.focus wid 4590 -> {"ev":"focus.mismatch","data":{"actual":3854,"requested":4590}} where 3854 is exactly the previously focused window.

confirmed.title: Directional focus dead-ends on empty cells instead of skipping them (noWindowsInCell spam on 'notify' cell)
confirmed.mechanism: moveFocus (GridFocus.swift:92) collects adjacency candidates (:136 adjacentMap[direction]) without filtering for cells that contain windows. pickClosestCell (:185, impl :766-792) selects purely by center distance — emptiness is never considered. The winner goes to focusCellByID (:188), which prunes dead windows and then throws GridFocusError.noWindowsInCell(cellID) when the cell is empty (:324-326). There is no retry with the next candidate, no skip-over to the cell beyond, and no wrap fallback after this throw, so the whole focus command fails. The cross-display path DOES filter to cellsWithWindows (:861-871), so the in-display path is the inconsistent one. The user's layout has a 'notify' cell (~/.config/thegrid/config.yaml:142) that is usually empty (its GridNotify panel window comes and goes — see the ax_orphan finding), so focus left/right toward it errors out repeatedly.

confirmed.title: Per-notification unstructured Task spawn loses event ordering — focus inversions and destroy-before-create for short-lived windows
confirmed.mechanism: AX notifications arrive in order on the main run loop but axNotificationCallback spawns an independent unstructured Task per notification (ApplicationObserver.swift:342-344 'Task { await appObserver.handleNotification(...) }'); WorkspaceObserver.applicationActivated does the same (WorkspaceObserver.swift:186-197, including a synchronous getFocusedWindowID AX query of variable latency inside the Task), and StateManager's poll routes its create/destroy batches in separate detached Tasks (StateManager.swift:1292-1300, 1323-1330). Tasks on the global executor have no ordering guarantee, so: (a) two rapid focus changes A-then-B can route B before A; StateManager.applyWindowFocus (StateManager.swift:754-758) overwrites metadata.focusedWindowID unconditionally — no sequence number — leaving the OLDER window recorded as focused, and the 300ms focusSweep (GridReconciler.swift:339-371) treats that cache as OS truth and actively enforces the stale window onto GridState/borders until the next genuine focus event; (b) for a fast create-close window (transient dialog, phantom) the Destroyed task — which does less AX work (:151-155) than the Created path's role query (:132-147) — can route windowDestroyed before windowCreated; StateManager processes the destroy as a no-op then handleWindowCreated (StateManager.swift:1446-1523) re-adds the dead window with no liveness check, and GridReconciler may assign the ghost to a cell until the 3s poll or validator removes it. EventRouter actor reentrancy compounds this: route() suspends at each 'try await handler.handle' (EventRouter.swift:205), so even in-order arrivals can interleave across handlers. The dispatch code is confirmed; specific end-to-end inversions are inferred from paired log mismatches.
confirmed.symptom: Focus border flips back to the previously focused window while the user is already typing in the new one (enforced by the sweep for up to 300ms cycles); ghost window briefly tracked/tiled after a transient dialog closes; spurious win.created after win.destroyed for the same wid; mismatch/retry bursts after rapid window churn.
confirmed.fixDirection: Funnel AX/workspace notifications through a single ordered pipeline (AsyncStream consumed by one task, or a serial actor queue) instead of one detached Task per callback, and stamp focus events with a monotonic sequence so applyWindowFocus rejects older-than-current events.

Logs: 51 sweep.correct events; adjacent inverted mismatch pairs {"ev":"focus.mismatch","data":{"actual":6439,"requested":6434,"retry":true},"ts":1781103105} / {"actual":6434,"requested":6439},"ts":1781103106}.

No serialization exists. (2) Asymmetric latency: the Created path does an extra AX role query (:132-147) before getWindowID, while Destroyed only does getWindowID (:151-155), so reordering pressure is real; note the destroy event only exists at all if getWindowID succeeds on the dying element (:152), which is the precondition, not a refutation. (3) WorkspaceObserver.swift:187-198 spawns the same pattern with a synchronous getFocusedWindowID AX query inside the Task. (4) EventRouter is an actor (EventRouter.swift:158) but route() does 'try await handler.handle(event, context:)' per handler (~:205) — actor reentrancy lets concurrent route() calls interleave at that await; there is no queue or sequence number. evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code precondition verified verbatim: ApplicationObserver.swift:341-344 spawns an unstructured Task per AX callback; WorkspaceObserver.swift:185-197 does the same with a variable-latency synchronous getFocusedWindowID AX query inside the Task; StateManager.swift:754-758 applyWindowFocus overwrites metadata.focusedWindowID unconditionally with no sequence guard; GridReconciler.swift:339-378 focusSweep reads that cache while its comment calls it 'OS-level focused window' and enforces it onto GridState/borders. Logs corroborate part (a): 146 '"ev":"focus.mismatch"' events in ~152k lines, including ping-pong bursts (ts 1780881708-1711: 8 mismatches in 3s rotating wids 3854/4590/4004; exact inverted adjacent pairs at ts 1781103105/106 and 1781043644/645), 51 sweep.correct corrections, and 12 focus.mismatch.accept events where the server gave up and accepted OS reality — these directly measure the cached focusedWindowID disagreeing with just-issued focus requests, matching the unordered-update mechanism. Part (b) (destroy-before-create ghost) is NOT supported by evidence: a scan of all 1050 win.created / 734 win.destroyed events found zero create-after-destroy pairs for the same wid within 5s; additionally all 734 destroys log app:"unknown" because the 3s poll removes windows from state synchronously before routing the destroy Task (StateManager.swift:1303-1330), meaning destroys are poll-driven and the AX-ordering inversion does not manifest in practice. Verdict confirmed on the primary focus-ordering mechanism; the ghost-window sub-claim should be treated as speculative. Severity stays medium: mismatch bursts are real and recurring (~daily during churn) but loop-detector/accept backstops bound the damage, and the part (b) absence argues against upgrading.
evidenceVerdict.addedEvidence: GridFocus.swift ~408: comment admitting the race — 'the macOS appActivated notification delivers focusedWindowID updates asynchronously; without this yield, the verification read can fire before the notification lands and report the *previous* focused window as actual, producing a spurious mismatch'. FocusLoopDetector.swift:5-7: 'Detects focus ping-pong... bail out of unbounded focus.mismatch retries when the OS keeps re-stealing focus'. Logs: 146 focus.mismatch total; burst ts 1780881708-1711 with 8 mismatches rotating 3854→4590→4004; inverted pairs ts 1781103105/106 and 1781043644/645; 12 focus.mismatch.accept; 51 sweep.correct; 0 focus.loop trips (3-window rotations evade the same-pair detector). Counter-evidence for part (b): 0 win.created-after-win.destroyed same-wid pairs within 5s across 1050 creates / 734 destroys; all 734 win.destroyed log app:"unknown" because poll removes window from state before routing destroy (StateManager.swift:1303-1330), showing destroys are poll-driven, not AX-race-prone.

confirmed.title: handleWindowMinimized removes the window from the focused display's space instead of the window's tracked space — minimized window keeps its cell slot
confirmed.mechanism: On .windowMinimized, the reconciler resolves 'currentSpaceID = await findCurrentSpaceIDAsync()' — metadata.activeSpaceID, i.e. the focused display's active space (GridReconciler.swift:1052, :1263-1275) — and calls gridState.removeWindow on THAT space (:1054). If the minimized window is tracked in a different space (yellow-button minimize on a second display's space, CLI/MCP window_minimize against any wid, or the event arriving after a space switch / stale activeSpaceID), GridState.removeWindow is a silent no-op (GridState.swift:381-385: guard + firstIndex(of:) never matches) and the window stays assigned to its cell. Neither validator pass can clean it up: pruneDeadWindows skips minimized windows (StateValidator.swift:210-212) and pruneAXOrphanedWindows skips them too (:242-244). The minimized window therefore permanently occupies a cell slot: applyCellLayout (GridApply.swift:331) includes it in split calculations and focus cycling can land on it. If the minimize event instead arrives during suppression it is dropped entirely (GridReconciler.swift:442), producing the same lingering assignment even on the correct space.
confirmed.symptom: After minimizing a window (especially on a non-focused display or via CLI), its cell still reserves a split for it: remaining windows stay half-width, cell ops compute splits for an invisible window, and focus cycle can target a Dock-minimized window until it is unminimized or destroyed.
confirmed.fixDirection: Use gridState.findSpaceContaining(windowID:) (as handleFocusChanged does at :848) to resolve the space to remove from, falling back to removeWindowFromAllSpaces.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:1048-1059: 'let currentSpaceID = await findCurrentSpaceIDAsync(); if let spaceID = currentSpaceID { await gridState.removeWindow(windowID, fromSpace: spaceID) ... }'. GridState.swift:381-385: 'guard var space = spaces[spaceID] else { return }; for (cellID, var cell) in space.cells { guard let idx = cell.windows.firstIndex(of: windowID) else { continue } ...' — no-op when window isn't in that space. StateValidator.swift:210 and :242 skip minimized windows in both prune passes.
confirmed.logSignature: "ev":"reconcile.win.min" for a wid that continues to appear in subsequent layout/border assignment logs

codeVerdict.reasoning: Independently re-traced every hop. (1) GridReconciler.swift:1048-1059 matches the finding verbatim: handleWindowMinimized calls findCurrentSpaceIDAsync (:1448-1452) which delegates to findCurrentSpaceID (:1263-1275) returning wmState.metadata.activeSpaceID — the focused display's active space, not the window's tracked space; no guard checks the window belongs to that space. (2) GridState.swift:381-385: removeWindow guards on spaces[spaceID] and uses firstIndex(of:)/continue — silent no-op when the window is tracked in a different space. (3) StateValidator.swift:210-212 (pruneDeadWindows) and :242-244 (pruneAXOrphanedWindows) both explicitly skip minimized windows, so neither validator pass can clean the stale assignment. (4) Hunted for counter-mechanisms the finder might have missed: sweepDisplacedWindows (GridReconciler.swift:1394-1446) cannot rescue — resolveDisplacedTarget (:1345) returns nil for empty actualSpaces (minimized), and it only migrates, never removes. (5) Suppression: GridReconciler.swift:441-443 drops .windowMinimized entirely during suppression (only focusChanged, pendingLaunch windowCreated, and spaceIDReassigned bypass the guard at :416-439) — no queue/replay, confirming the secondary mechanism. (7) ApplicationObserver.swift:236-238 emits windowMinimized from per-app kAXWindowMiniaturizedNotification with no display/focus gating, so minimize on a non-focused display's space is a real trigger. (8) git log -8 on the file shows no commits after 713cf7a (#63, pre-audit); code unchanged. Actor isolation is irrelevant — this is a wrong-space resolution, not a data race. Only inaccuracy found: "permanently occupies a cell slot" overstates persistence — a full applyLayout (grid_layout_apply/cycle/refresh, or display reconnect via refreshAllDisplays at GridApply.swift:393-445) re-derives assignments via filterTileableFromState (GridApply.swift:159, :539-547; minimized windows fail both the spaces.contains(spaceIDInt) check and isTileable at GridAssignment.swift:110) and wholesale-replaces them via setWindowAssignments (GridApply.swift:266), purging the stale entry. codeVerdict.addedEvidence: Counter-mechanism that bounds (but does not negate) the bug: GridApply.swift:120-272 applyLayoutBody re-derives assignments from filterTileableFromState (:159, :528-559 — requires windowState.spaces.contains(spaceIDInt) at :541 and isTileable at :547, both false for minimized windows per GridAssignment.swift:110) and replaces state wholesale via gridState.setWindowAssignments (:266); refreshAllDisplays (:393-445) routes through the same path. So the stale assignment heals on the next full layout apply/refresh/cycle for that space — "permanently" in the finding should read "until unminimize, destroy, or next full layout apply". Also: sweepDisplacedWindows (GridReconciler.swift:1394) cannot clean it because resolveDisplacedTarget:1345 returns nil for empty actualSpaces (minimized), and it only migrates between spaces, never removes. Event origin confirmed: ApplicationObserver.swift:236-238 fires StateEvent.windowMinimized from kAXWindowMiniaturizedNotification per-app with no display/focus gate.

confirmed.title: pid-less pendingLaunchTarget claimable by any app's window — and a silently failed picker launch leaves it armed for 15s
confirmed.mechanism: After a picker selection, PickerManager.handleResult arms the launch target BEFORE executing the action (PickerManager.swift:221-228 capturedOnLaunch(action) -> GridCommandRouter.swift:616-629 setPendingLaunchTarget with pid:nil); pid stays nil until NSWorkspace's launch completion fires updatePendingLaunchTargetPID (GridReconciler.swift:197-201). During that gap, handle() routes EVERY .windowCreated to handlePendingLaunchWindow even during suppression (:423-428), and the rejectedWindowSweep (:404-408) and handleWindowMoved un-reject path (:1041-1045) do the same for maturing rejected windows. In handlePendingLaunchWindow the PID guard is explicitly skipped when target.pid is nil (:708 'if let targetPID = target.pid, pid != targetPID'), so any tileable, non-modal window from ANY app appearing on the target space (or moved there by moveWindowToSpace at :771) consumes the target at :799, is prepended to the target cell (:800), and focused (:807); the real picked app's window later falls through to ordinary auto-assign. A previously-rejected 0x0 phantom maturing on the ~300ms sweep is a realistic claimant during app-launch latency. The failure path makes this worse: ActionExecutor's .openApp case (ActionExecutor.swift:31-45) has NO else branch when urlForApplication fails (uninstalled app / stale history entry) — no log, no target cleanup — and the openApplication error completion (:37-39) logs pick.err.open but also never clears the target. The target then stays armed with pid:nil for the full 15s timeout (GridReconciler.swift:52, checked only lazily at :719-726), guaranteed to hijack the next unrelated window the user opens.
confirmed.symptom: Picker places and focuses the wrong window in the chosen cell while the picked app lands elsewhere unfocused; after picking an app that fails to launch, a window opened by any other means within 15 seconds gets teleported into the picker's target cell with focus forced onto it.
confirmed.fixDirection: Buffer candidate windows until the launch PID arrives (or match on the picked app's bundle ID) instead of letting the first tileable window claim a pid-less target; in ActionExecutor .openApp add an else branch that logs and clears the pending target, and clear it on openApplication error.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:704-708: '// If target.pid is nil (NSWorkspace completion hasn't fired yet), skip the PID check -- multi-shot skipping on isTileable/classifyWindow is sufficient until PID arrives.\n if let targetPID = target.pid, pid != targetPID {'. Claim at :799-801: 'pendingLaunchTarget = nil; await gridState.prependWindow(windowID, toCellID: target.cellID, ...); await gridState.setFocus(...)'. ActionExecutor.swift:31-45: 'case .openApp(let bundleID): if let url = NSWorkspace.shared.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier: bundleID) { ... }' — no else. Log shows 13 reconcile.pending.set and 0 reconcile.pending.expired.

(2) Routing: GridReconciler.swift:421-428 routes every .windowCreated to handlePendingLaunchWindow whenever a target is armed, deliberately BEFORE the suppression guard; the 300ms sweep timer (:321-329) calls rejectedWindowSweep which feeds matured rejected windows into the same handler (:404-405), as does handleWindowMoved's un-reject path (:1041-1042). confirmed.title: pendingLaunchTarget double-consumption: check-then-consume spans multiple awaits between the sweep and event paths
confirmed.mechanism: Two independent paths call handlePendingLaunchWindow: the EventRouter windowCreated path (GridReconciler.swift:423-428, checked BEFORE the suppression guard) and the 300ms timer's rejectedWindowSweep (:404-408) when a previously-rejected phantom becomes tileable. handlePendingLaunchWindow reads pendingLaunchTarget at :698, then performs multiple awaits (getState :730, layout check :791) before consuming the target at :799 ('pendingLaunchTarget = nil') and prepending+focusing (:800-807). Both invocations can interleave inside that window: both observe target non-nil, both pass the PID check (same launched app — the unrejected former phantom and the real window; or target.pid still nil per :706-707), and both prepend their window to target.cellID, double-applying the cell layout and fighting over focus. Note this is NOT fully fixed by converting GridReconciler to an actor: actor reentrancy still allows interleaving across the awaits between the :698 read and the :799 consume — the consume must move before the first await.
confirmed.symptom: After launching an app from the picker, two windows of that app (one being the recovered phantom) both land in the chosen cell, or focus jumps twice; the picker target cell ends up with an unexpected extra window.
confirmed.fixDirection: Consume (or mark in-flight) the pending target before the first await in handlePendingLaunchWindow, restoring it on the skip paths.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:404-408 (sweep path): 'if pendingLaunchTarget != nil { await handlePendingLaunchWindow(wid, windowState.pid) }'; :697-699 'guard let target = pendingLaunchTarget else {...}'; many awaits later :799 'pendingLaunchTarget = nil' then :800 prependWindow. Comment at :706-707 concedes PID may be nil during the race window.
confirmed.logSignature: "ev":"reconcile.win.create.picker" twice within the same second, or "ev":"sweep.unrejected" immediately followed by "ev":"reconcile.win.create.picker"

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-read GridReconciler.swift and traced every hop. (1) Sweep path exists verbatim: rejectedWindowSweep at :384-409 calls handlePendingLaunchWindow(wid, pid) at :404-405 when pendingLaunchTarget != nil, after unrejecting a now-tileable phantom at :395-397. (2) Event path at :421-428 checks pendingLaunchTarget BEFORE the suppression guard (:442) and calls handlePendingLaunchWindow. (3) handlePendingLaunchWindow reads the target at :698, then suspends at :730 (await stateProvider.getState(), StateManager actor hop) and :791 (await gridState.getCurrentLayout, GridState actor hop) before consuming at :799 (pendingLaunchTarget = nil) and prepending/focusing at :800-807. (4) PID check at :708 passes for both windows of the same launched app; nil-PID skip concession at :706-707 is real. (5) Phantoms genuinely enter the rejected set: handleWindowCreated :588-589 calls gridState.rejectWindow on non-tileable windows, so the sweep-side trigger is live. (6) Concurrency holds — and is worse than claimed: GridReconciler is a plain class (:21), not an actor; the sweep runs in an unstructured Task spawned from a DispatchSource timer handler (:317-330) on the global concurrent executor, while the event path arrives via the EventRouter actor awaiting the nonisolated async handle (EventRouter.swift:205) — separate tasks, zero shared isolation, Package.swift is swift-tools-version 5.9 with no strict concurrency. Refutation attempts failed: the sweep's suppression guard (:385) doesn't protect the loop because handlePick (GridCommandRouter.swift:604-635) does not hold suppression across the app-launch wait (target lives up to 15s, :52); the 284fe6a 'picker dedup' (already_assigned check :614-621) is in handleWindowCreated, not handlePendingLaunchWindow, and the race involves two distinct window IDs; git log shows no later fix (HEAD for this file is 713cf7a) and the cited lines match the finding exactly. All skip paths (:708, :733, :738, :753) deliberately do not consume the target, keeping it alive for double consumption. confirmed.title: sweepDisplacedWindows migrates a window's cell assignment but never repositions it
confirmed.mechanism: When sweepDisplacedWindows (GridReconciler.swift:1394-1446) detects a window whose OS space differs from its tracked space, it does 'await gridState.removeWindow(wid, fromSpace: trackedSpaceID); await gridState.assignWindow(wid, toCellID: targetCell, inSpace: targetSpaceID)' (:1425-1426) and then only syncBordersForSpace (:1439-1445). It never calls gridApply.applyCellLayout for either the source or the target cell, unlike every other assignment path (locked assign at :642/:663; picker path at :804). The migrated window keeps its pre-migration frame, and the windows remaining in the source cell as well as the existing windows in the target cell keep their old split geometry computed for the old member counts.
confirmed.symptom: After a window moves across spaces (or gets force-migrated by the deriveSpaceFromDisplay bug), it is logically a cell member — border drawn, focus navigation includes it — but physically sits at its old frame overlapping other cells; co-cell windows keep stale split sizes until the user reapplies the layout.
confirmed.fixDirection: After migrating, call applyCellLayout for the target cell (and the vacated source cell) so geometry matches the new assignments.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:1425-1433: 'await gridState.removeWindow(wid, fromSpace: trackedSpaceID)\n await gridState.assignWindow(wid, toCellID: targetCell, inSpace: targetSpaceID)\n jlog("reconcile.lift.migrate", ...)' — the only follow-up is syncBordersForSpace at :1444. Log: {"ev":"reconcile.lift.migrate","data":{"cell":"right","from":"6","to":"3","wid":5735},"ts":1780805484} with no layout.cell event following for that cell.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop at HEAD (latest commit touching file: 713cf7a; finding's line numbers match exactly). (1) sweepDisplacedWindows at GridReconciler.swift:1394-1446 does removeWindow/assignWindow at :1425-1426 and its only follow-up is syncBordersForSpace at :1444 — no gridApply.applyCellLayout anywhere in the function. (2) syncBordersForSpace (:1170-1259) cannot reposition windows: it computes the layout only to validate it (`_ = GridLayout.calculateLayoutWithRatios` at :1217) and ends in borderRenderer.setCellAssignments (:1249). (3) GridState.assignWindow/removeWindow (GridState.swift:326/:381) are pure state mutations; markDirty (:128-139) only debounce-persists JSON. (4) The three callers of sweepDisplacedWindows (:110, :122, :154) follow it only with syncBordersForCurrentSpace. (5) Contrast paths confirmed: locked-assign at :641-642 and :660-663 and picker path at :800-804 all pair assignment with applyCellLayout, which physically computes placements (GridApply.swift:298+). (6) Hunted for self-heal and found none: the 300ms sweep timer (:325-330) runs only focusSweep (focus-state correction, :339-379) and rejectedWindowSweep (:384+); handleSpaceChanged (:895-908) only syncs borders on space switch. So a migrated window stays at its old frame and co-cell windows keep stale split geometry until the user manually reapplies a layout. No guard, debounce, or actor-isolation argument refutes this — it is a straightforward omission, not a race.

confirmed.title: Locked-rule window assigned to a cell on an inactive space is never placed there and gets bounced back by the displacement sweep
confirmed.mechanism: When a locked app's window is created and the locked cell only exists on another space, handleWindowCreated assigns it there in GridState (GridReconciler.swift:660) but findDisplayUUIDForSpace (:1309-1316) only matches a display whose currentSpaceID equals that space. If the locked cell's space is NOT currently visible on any display, displayUUID is nil, so the 'if let displayUUID' block (:662-665) skips applyCellLayout — the window is never positioned or moved to the target space, while reconcile.win.create.locked is still logged (:666-672) as if it succeeded. wmState keeps reporting the window on its original space, so the next action-exit sweepDisplacedWindows (:1394-1446) sees tracked=lockedSpace vs actual=[originalSpace] and migrates it into the focused cell of the original space (:1423-1426), silently defeating the locked rule. No retry ever re-applies the rule because windowCreated only fires once.
confirmed.symptom: An app with a locked cell rule launches while that cell's space is in the background: its window stays on the wrong space in an arbitrary cell, never reaching the reserved cell.
confirmed.fixDirection: When the locked cell's space is not the current space of any display, move the window to that space via windowController.moveWindowToSpace before assigning, or defer the locked assignment until the space becomes active.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-read GridReconciler.swift:638-676 (locked-rule branch of handleWindowCreated), :1309-1316 (findDisplayUUIDForSpace), :1339-1358 (resolveDisplacedTarget), :1394-1446 (sweepDisplacedWindows), :99-155 (executeAction/endAction depth-0 exits that invoke the sweep), :895-908 (handleSpaceChanged — borders only, no rescue), plus GridApply.swift:298-387 (applyCellLayout) and GridState.swift:326-343/520-530/568-580 (assignWindow, findSpaceContaining, getAllWindowIDs). Every hop holds: assignment at :660 is unconditional; placement at :662-665 is gated on findDisplayUUIDForSpace which matches only displays whose currentSpaceID equals the target space, so a background space yields nil and skips applyCellLayout; the success log at :666-672 fires regardless; there is no retry path. Attempted refutations all failed: (a) the only moveWindowToSpace in the reconciler is :771 inside handlePendingLaunchWindow (picker path only); (b) applyCellLayout itself never moves windows across spaces — it only sets AX frames via applyPlacementsViaAX (GridApply.swift:383), so the inactive-space case has no transport mechanism at all; (c) handleSpaceChanged only syncs borders when the space becomes active — no rule re-application; (d) no race is needed — sweepDisplacedWindows is serialized after the assignment and, per its conservative design, migrates the window TOWARD its actual OS space (originalSpace, which is tracked since handleWindowCreated bailed at :583 unless it had a layout), assigning it to getFocusedCell ?? "left" (:1423-1426) without consulting locked rules; (e) git log shows the file last changed in 713cf7a (in HEAD), and the cited lines match the finding verbatim. Even without the sweep, the window is never placed in or moved to the locked cell, so the symptom holds independently.

confirmed.title: Reconciler space-change handling is dead code: FocusState.previous* never populated and spaceSwitched events carry nil windowID
confirmed.mechanism: GridReconciler.handleFocusChanged detects a space change via 'focusState.previousSpaceID != nil && previousSpaceID != spaceID && spaceID != 0' (GridReconciler.swift:866-868) and only then calls its handleSpaceChanged border-sync (:871, defined :895-908). But FocusState.previousSpaceID/previousWindowID are never set anywhere in the codebase — every constructor call (ApplicationObserver.swift:176-191, WorkspaceObserver.swift:135-139 and 190-195) uses the nil defaults from the convenience init (EventRouter.swift:74-91). Additionally the spaceSwitched event from WorkspaceObserver.spaceChanged has windowID nil, so handleFocusChanged bails at its first guard (:816 'guard ... let windowID = focusState.windowID else { return }'). Net: the reconciler's intended on-space-switch border/layout sync path is unreachable; space switches currently get borders synced only as a side effect of the buggy spaceIDReassigned migration (GridReconciler.swift:929) or a later incidental focus event/sweep. Fixing the spurious-migration finding without fixing this leaves space switches with no sync path at all.
confirmed.symptom: After switching spaces, borders/focus highlight are stale or missing until the next focus change or a 300ms sweep mismatch — and would be permanently unsynced if the spurious migration path were fixed.
confirmed.fixDirection: Handle the spaceSwitched trigger explicitly in handleFocusChanged (don't require windowID), or populate FocusState.previous* fields at the event source.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:816 'guard let gridState, let stateProvider, let windowID = focusState.windowID else { return }'; :866 'let spaceChanged = focusState.previousSpaceID != nil ...'. grep for 'previousSpaceID' shows zero writers outside EventRouter.swift defaults. Log: grep -c '"ev":"reconcile.space.change"' = 0 across 150k lines despite 122 spc.changed events.
