confirmed.title: createObserver registration TOCTOU — duplicate AXObservers and dangling refcon after wake rebuild
confirmed.mechanism: createObserver guards 'applicationObservers[pid] == nil' (StateManager.swift:1196) but the observer is only inserted into the dictionary later, after a fire-and-forget 'Task { @MainActor in if observer.observe(...) { await self.addApplicationObserver(...) } }' completes (:1202-1206 -> :1210-1212). Any second createObserver for the same pid during that async window passes the nil guard and creates a second live AXObserver. Realistic trigger: handleSystemWoke -> rebuildAXObservers (:2083-2101) spawns one MainActor Task per app; an appLaunched event (:1945 -> createObserver) or a second wake/rebuild arriving before those Tasks finish re-creates observers for the same pids. Both observers register run-loop sources with refcon = Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) (ApplicationObserver.swift:61). When addApplicationObserver overwrites the dict entry (:1211), the displaced ApplicationObserver is released WITHOUT stopObserving() — its run-loop source and unretained refcon pointer remain installed, so a subsequent AX callback dereferences a dangling pointer (ApplicationObserver.swift:341 takeUnretainedValue). Best case: duplicate event delivery; worst case: use-after-free crash on the main thread.
confirmed.symptom: Doubled AX events (duplicate ev.win.create / ev.focus per real event) after wake; rare main-thread crash in AX callback shortly after wake or app-launch storms.
confirmed.fixDirection: Reserve the dict slot synchronously (insert a placeholder) before spawning the MainActor Task, and stopObserving() any observer being replaced in addApplicationObserver.
confirmed.evidence: StateManager.swift:1196 'guard applicationObservers[pid] == nil else { return }'; :1202-1206 'Task { @MainActor in if observer.observe(stateManager: self) { await self.addApplicationObserver(observer, for: pid) } }'; :1210-1212 silently overwrites; ApplicationObserver.swift:61 'let context = Unmanaged.passUnretained(self).toOpaque()'.
confirmed.logSignature: duplicate "ev":"ax.observer.create" for same pid without intervening "ax.observer.stop"

codeVerdict.reasoning: I set out to refute this and could not — every cited line says exactly what the finding claims, and no guard, debounce, or isolation closes the window. (1) StateManager is an actor (StateManager.swift:16), so dictionary access is serialized, but that does NOT serialize the race: createObserver checks `guard applicationObservers[pid] == nil` at :1196, then spawns a fire-and-forget `Task { @MainActor in if observer.observe(...) { await self.addApplicationObserver(...) } }` at :1202-1206; the insertion (:1211) happens only after a MainActor hop plus an actor hop back. Between the guard and the insertion, dict[pid] is nil while a live observer is in flight — a second createObserver for the same pid in that window passes the guard. (2) The trigger path is real: handleSystemWoke (:2058) → rebuildAXObservers (:2083) stops all observers, removeAll (:2092), then observeExistingApplications (:1174) spawns one fire-and-forget Task per app and rebuildAXObservers returns WITHOUT awaiting them. Worse than the finding states, the actor is re-entrant at suspension points: handleSystemWoke suspends 2s at Task.sleep (:2067) and rebuildAXObservers suspends at `await MainActor.run` per observer (:2088), so an appLaunched event (handle switch at :240-241 → handleApplicationLaunched :1934 → createObserver :1945) or a second wake can interleave while rebuild Tasks for the same pids are pending. (3) observe() has no already-observing guard (ApplicationObserver.swift:36-108) — a duplicate observer registers all 8 notifications with refcon = Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) (:61) and adds its run-loop source to the main run loop (:97). (4) addApplicationObserver (:1210-1212) is a bare `applicationObservers[pid] = observer` — the displaced observer is never stopObserving()'d, and I grepped ApplicationObserver.swift for `deinit`: there is none, so CFRunLoopRemoveSource (:115) and notification removal never happen for the displaced instance. The run loop retains the CFRunLoopSource, so callbacks keep arriving with a refcon pointing at the deallocated Swift wrapper, dereferenced via takeUnretainedValue at :341 — use-after-free; before dealloc, two live observers means doubled event delivery. (5) git log shows no recent change to this code (last 8 commits touch unrelated areas; :1196/:1202/:1211 match the finding verbatim). The only probabilistic element is trigger timing (a pid must hit the in-flight window), which is why severity medium — not the mechanism, which holds end-to-end.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: Stronger than the finding claims: (a) the actor is re-entrant — handleSystemWoke suspends for 2 full seconds at StateManager.swift:2067 (`try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 2_000_000_000)`) and rebuildAXObservers suspends at :2088 (`await MainActor.run { observer.stopObserving() }`) once per existing observer, giving many interleave points for appLaunched/second-wake events mid-rebuild, not just after it. (b) ApplicationObserver has NO deinit (verified by grep over /Users/r/repos/theGrid/grid-server/Sources/GridServer/ApplicationObserver.swift), so a displaced observer's run-loop source (added at :97) is never removed — the cleanup path :111-125 is only reachable via explicit stopObserving(), which addApplicationObserver (:1210-1212) never calls on overwrite. (c) The rebuild log at :2097-2100 reports `"new": applicationObservers.count` immediately after spawning the fire-and-forget Tasks, so it logs a near-zero count — a corroborating log signature ("ax.observer.rebuild" with new << old) in addition to the finding's duplicate "ax.observer.create" signature.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code actively demonstrates every step of the claimed mechanism: StateManager.swift:1196 guards 'applicationObservers[pid] == nil' but the insert happens later via fire-and-forget 'Task { @MainActor in ... await self.addApplicationObserver }' (:1202-1206), and StateManager is an actor (line 16) so a second createObserver for the same pid can pass the guard in that window; addApplicationObserver (:1210-1212) silently overwrites without calling stopObserving() on the displaced observer; ApplicationObserver.swift has NO deinit (grep confirmed), so the displaced observer's run-loop source (added at ApplicationObserver.swift:97) stays installed with refcon = Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) (:61), dereferenced via takeUnretainedValue() in axNotificationCallback (:341) — a genuine dangling-pointer path. confirmed.title: StateManager actor blocked by synchronous AX IPC — no AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout anywhere
confirmed.mechanism: Every poll tick, updateWindowFromPoll re-queries AX properties for EVERY window whose role is nil (StateManager.swift:1353-1367) synchronously on the StateManager actor. getAXProperties (:549-599) issues several blocking AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue/_AXUIElementGetWindow IPC calls; the codebase never calls AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout (grep: 0 hits), so each call to an unresponsive/beachballing app blocks for the system default (~6s). Phantom nil-role windows are exactly the windows owned by misbehaving apps, and several can exist per app, so a single hung app can stall the actor for tens of seconds per poll tick. While blocked, every 'await stateProvider.getState()' — issued by GridCommandRouter for every hotkey (GridCommandRouter.swift:167+), by focusSweep (GridReconciler.swift:344), and by handleFocusChanged — queues behind the actor: the entire window manager freezes. refreshAXPropertiesForActiveSpace (:987-1011, run on every space change) and handleWindowCreated's getAXProperties (:1483) have the same blocking shape.
confirmed.symptom: All hotkeys and border updates freeze for seconds at a time whenever any app stops responding (app launch, heavy load, beachball), recovering when the app does.
confirmed.fixDirection: Call AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout (e.g. 0.5s) on app elements, and/or perform AX property queries off-actor (like the CGWindowList snapshot already is) and apply results in a second actor hop.
confirmed.evidence: StateManager.swift:1355-1356 '// Re-query AX properties when role is nil ... let axProps = getAXProperties(pid: window.pid, windowID: windowID)' inside applyPollResults (actor-isolated); getAXProperties:553-558 synchronous AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue; 'grep -rn AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout Sources/GridServer' returns nothing.
confirmed.logSignature: gap of several seconds between consecutive "ev":"win.refresh" / poll events while srv requests stall

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop in code. (1) StateManager.swift:16 declares `actor StateManager`. (2) startPolling (StateManager.swift:1235-1248) fires every 3s; the comment at :1241 explicitly moves the CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo call off-actor 'to avoid blocking', but then `await self?.applyPollResults(windowList)` (:1247) hops back onto the actor, and applyPollResults → updateWindowFromPoll (:1275, :1337) calls getAXProperties at :1355-1356 for every window with `role == nil`, exactly as claimed. (3) getAXProperties (:549-599) issues synchronous AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue (:554) and _AXUIElementGetWindow (:568, :588) plus further synchronous copies in extractAXProperties (:629) — all blocking Mach IPC executed actor-isolated. (4) `grep -rn AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` across the entire repo returns 0 hits, so the macOS default ~6s AX messaging timeout applies (the 6s figure is documented OS behavior, the only hop not verifiable in code). (5) No suppression/backoff exists: :1357 only sets role on success, so a hung app's windows remain nil-role and are re-queried every tick indefinitely; refreshAXPropertiesForActiveSpace (:987-1011, invoked on space change at :1791) and handleWindowCreated (:1483) share the identical blocking shape. (6) Stall propagation verified: getState() (:137) is actor-isolated; GridCommandRouter.swift awaits it at :306, :311, :571, :586, :638 (finding cited ':167+' — call sites are actually at 306+, a minor line discrepancy that does not affect the mechanism) and GridReconciler.swift focusSweep awaits stateProvider.getState() at :339-344 plus :391, :510, :556, :730, :851, :859. Git log for StateManager.swift (1cf354e, 713cf7a, etc.) shows recent phantom-window work but no timeout was ever added and AX calls were never moved off-actor. I looked specifically for an early return, a retry cap, a debounce, or off-actor execution of the AX queries and found none — the actor serializes awaiters behind the blocked call rather than protecting against it.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: StateManager.swift:1240-1247 — the poll timer comment 'Perform heavy CGWindowList call outside actor to avoid blocking' shows the authors already treat actor-blocking as a hazard and solved it for CGWindowList, yet the AX IPC in applyPollResults/updateWindowFromPoll runs on the actor anyway; this both corroborates the finding and confirms the proposed fixDirection (off-actor query + second actor hop) matches the existing pattern. Additional unlisted stall points: GridReconciler.swift awaits getState at :391, :510, :556, :730, :851, :859 beyond the cited focusSweep:344, and GridCommandRouter at :306, :311, :571, :586, :638 (the cited :167 does not contain a getState call, but five other lines do).

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code actively demonstrates the mechanism: StateManager.swift:16 declares `actor StateManager`; updateWindowFromPoll (:1337) is actor-isolated and at :1355-1356 calls getAXProperties for every nil-role window on every 3s poll tick (startPolling interval 3.0 at :134; only the CGWindowList snapshot at :1240-1248 is off-actor — applyPollResults hops back onto the actor). getAXProperties (:549-599) issues synchronous AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue plus a per-window _AXUIElementGetWindow loop. Repo-wide grep for AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout/setMessagingTimeout returns 0 hits, so the ~6s system default applies per call to a hung app. GridCommandRouter.swift:306,311,571,586,638 all `await stateManager.getState()`, confirming hotkeys queue behind the actor; refreshAXPropertiesForActiveSpace (:987-1011) has the identical blocking loop on space change. HOWEVER, log evidence shows the bug has never observably fired: ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json spans ~10 days (152,843 lines, ts 1780352807-1781205415). StateValidator.swift:148-153 shows each 30s validator tick performs `await stateProvider.getState()` BEFORE jlog("validate.start"), making the 28,421 validate ticks a responsiveness probe of the StateManager actor: zero validate.start->validate.end deltas >= 2s, and only 4 inter-tick gaps >= 35s (46/41/66/39s); inspecting log context inside each gap shows other actor-crossing events (win.focus, bdr.rebuild, cmd.dispatch) processed with same-second latency, so those gaps are DispatchSourceTimer leeway/idle, not actor stalls. confirmed.title: GridFocus.focusLoopDetector mutated from concurrent contexts (array data race)
confirmed.mechanism: GridFocus is a plain class holding 'private var focusLoopDetector = FocusLoopDetector()' (GridFocus.swift:63), a struct whose mutating observe() does recent.removeAll + recent.append (FocusLoopDetector.swift:56-62). focusWindowByID calls focusLoopDetector.observe at GridFocus.swift:432 and is invoked concurrently from: (a) the command path — each socket request Task via GridCommandRouter -> moveFocus/cycleFocus (GridFocus.swift:242, 261, 359); (b) GridReconciler.handlePendingLaunchWindow on the event path (GridReconciler.swift:807); (c) the 300ms rejectedWindowSweep which can reach handlePendingLaunchWindow (GridReconciler.swift:404-408). Two overlapping calls mutate the 'recent' Array without synchronization — Array CoW reallocation under concurrent mutation is undefined behavior (possible crash) and at minimum corrupts loop-detection counts so ping-pong bail-out misfires or never trips. Distinct from the GridReconciler isolation finding: GridFocus is a separate unisolated class.
confirmed.symptom: Focus mismatch retry storms that the loop detector should have stopped (unbounded focus ping-pong between two windows), or a rare crash inside FocusLoopDetector.observe during simultaneous picker-launch and hotkey focus.
confirmed.fixDirection: Isolate GridFocus (or at least the detector) to an actor; it is only ever used via await already.
confirmed.evidence: GridFocus.swift:63 'private var focusLoopDetector = FocusLoopDetector()'; :432 'if let trip = focusLoopDetector.observe(requested: windowID, actual: actualWID, now: ...)'; FocusLoopDetector.swift:47 'mutating func observe' with :56 'recent.removeAll {...}' and :62 'recent.append(...)'; GridReconciler.swift:807 calls it from the event path. Log shows 146 focus.mismatch events feeding this path.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop. (1) GridFocus is a plain nonisolated class (GridFocus.swift:47) holding 'private var focusLoopDetector = FocusLoopDetector()' (:63); observe() is mutating and does recent.removeAll/append on a plain Array (FocusLoopDetector.swift:47,56-62); called at GridFocus.swift:432 in focusWindowByID's mismatch branch (:421). (2) Command path is genuinely concurrent: MessageHandler (plain class, MessageHandler.swift:12) spawns one unstructured Task per RPC at :1389 calling router.dispatch; dispatch (GridCommandRouter.swift:158-210) has no lock or queue — its only gate is awaitWakeCompletion. (3) The strongest refutation candidate — executeAction wrapping focus commands (GridCommandRouter.swift:176) — is NOT a serializer: it is ref-counted suppression ('suppressionDepth += 1', GridReconciler.swift:91-129, comment at :54-57 says multiple callers can nest), so two concurrent focus RPCs both run focusWindowByID in parallel on the global concurrent executor. (4) Event path: GridReconciler.swift:807 calls gridFocus?.focusWindowByID from handlePendingLaunchWindow, reachable from windowCreated events that explicitly bypass suppression (:423-427 'must be claimed even during move suppression') and from the 300ms sweep whose DispatchSource handler spawns unstructured Tasks (:317-330); the suppressReconciliation guard at :385 is a point-in-time check, not mutual exclusion. EventRouter is an actor but awaits nonisolated handler.handle and is reentrant at that await. (5) No compiler protection: Package.swift is swift-tools-version 5.9, Swift 5 mode, no defaultIsolation or strict-concurrency flags. (6) git log shows GridFocus.swift unchanged in this region since 817ca24; current code matches the finding. The only mitigating factor is that observe() is reached solely on focus mismatch, so the race needs two overlapping mismatching focus calls — but that is precisely the ping-pong-storm scenario the detector exists for, and missing happens-before edges also mean counts written by one thread may never be visible to another, supporting the 'detector never trips' symptom even without exact simultaneity. Minor citation nit: GridFocus.swift:242/:261 are in cycleFocus and :359 is focusCellByID (reached from moveFocus via :188); mechanism unaffected.

Its only failure branch (GetProcessForPID fails, :461-464) routes to focusWindowFallback (:485-497) which also discards mssClient results and returns true unconditionally (:496). Worse, focusWindow(context:) (:513-519) runs 'await context.stateManager.setFocusedWindow(context.windowID)' on this always-true result, so when focus actually failed (AX element nil at :477 — getAXElement already returned nil so no raise happened; or SLPS .failure because the symbol failed to load, MacOSAPIs.swift:279) StateManager records the window as focused, moves activeDisplay/activeSpace (StateManager.swift:797-830), and border sync follows the phantom focus.

confirmed.title: MSSClient availability cache is permanent: resetAvailabilityCache() has zero callers
confirmed.mechanism: MSSClient.isAvailable (MSSClient.swift:106-147) probes mss_handshake up to 3 times on first call and then caches the verdict forever (cachedAvailable :99, set at :124/:143). The escape hatch resetAvailabilityCache() (:150-154) is documented as 'call on system wake to re-probe MSS' but a repo-wide grep finds NO callers — StateManager.handleSystemWoke (StateManager.swift:2058-2078) refreshes state and rebuilds AX observers but never touches MSS. Consequences for the long-lived MSSClient instances (StateManager's own and the single WindowManipulator built in main.swift:194): (a) if the handshake fails once at startup (observed: mss.fail err:-3 x3 then mss.unavailable at ts 1780353154; mss.available has 0 hits in the whole log), MSS is treated as absent for the entire server lifetime — every moveWindowToSpace permanently takes the degraded direct-SLS path (WindowManipulator.swift:393-402, 20 warn.mss fallback hits); (b) conversely a cached-true client whose Dock-side socket died (Dock restart) keeps returning true at :108-110 without re-handshaking, so every space move fails until server restart.
confirmed.symptom: Window-to-space moves silently use the unreliable SkyLight fallback (or fail outright after a Dock restart) for the rest of the session; recovery requires restarting grid-server even though MSS is healthy again.
confirmed.fixDirection: Call resetAvailabilityCache() from the wake handler (and on repeated mss.fail of real operations trigger a re-probe/reconnect) instead of leaving the cache permanent.
confirmed.evidence: MSSClient.swift:149-154: '/// Reset availability cache (call on system wake to re-probe MSS)\n func resetAvailabilityCache() { queue.sync { cachedAvailable = nil } }' — grep -rn resetAvailabilityCache returns only the definition and doc comment. StateManager handleSystemWoke (2058-2078) has no MSS call. Log: {"ev":"mss.fail","data":{"attempt":3,"err":-3,"op":"handshake"}} then mss.unavailable; mss.available count 0; warn.mss not_available count 20 including recent ts 1781151535.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop independently. (1) Permanent cache: MSSClient.swift:108-110 early-returns cachedAvailable; set at :124/:143; reconnect() only reachable inside the initial probe loop. (2) Zero callers: repo-wide grep for resetAvailabilityCache hits only the definition (MSSClient.swift:150) and its doc comment (:103) plus identical worktree copies — no call site. (3) StateManager.handleSystemWoke (StateManager.swift:2058-2078) does only a 2s sleep, refreshCompleteState(), and rebuildAXObservers() — no mssClient reference, confirmed by grep of the whole function. (4) WindowManipulator.swift:360 gates moveWindowToSpace on mssClient.isAvailable(); else-branch :394-402 logs warn.mss not_available and falls back to moveWindowViaSkyLightAPI; the manipulator is built once at main.swift:194 with its own MSSClient (WindowManipulator.swift:51), so the cached-false verdict is session-permanent. (5) Logs corroborate: mss.available 0 hits, mss.unavailable 1, warn.mss not_available 20 hits spanning ~9 days after the single failed probe. (6) git log shows no recent change to MSSClient.swift adding a caller (last touch eb6a108). The only unverifiable piece is the secondary sub-claim about Dock-restart breaking a cached-true client: the no-re-handshake behavior is code-verified, but libmss is an external binary (pkgConfig 'mss', headers only at grid-server/include/mss/), so its persistent-vs-per-call connection model is unknown; this does not affect the headline mechanism. Notably, the author's own comments (:96-98, :103-104) state the wake-reset was intended — it was simply never wired up.

This strengthens the finding: a possibly transient connect failure at ts 1780353154 permanently disabled MSS, with 20 warn.mss SkyLight fallbacks observed through ts 1781151535 (~9 days later). Also: MSSClient.moveWindowToSpace (MSSClient.swift:182-197) and all other ops never call reconnect() on failure — reconnect is exclusively reachable from the one-time probe loop in isAvailable().

confirmed.title: BFD config watcher silently dies after first atomic-save (rename) and never re-arms
confirmed.mechanism: BFDManager.startConfigWatcher (BFDManager.swift:162-194) opens the config file fd exactly once at startup ('let fd = open(expandedPath, O_EVTONLY)', :164) and installs a DispatchSource with eventMask [.write, .delete, .rename, .extend]. The event handler (:173-187) only debounces and calls reload(); it never cancels and recreates the watcher. When an editor saves via atomic rename (vim, VS Code safe write), the watched inode is renamed/deleted: the source fires once (one final reload), but the fd now references a dead inode, so every subsequent edit to the new file at the same path produces no events — hotkey config changes are silently ignored until server restart. Additionally :165 'guard fd >= 0 else { return }' bails with no log if the file is missing at startup. Contrast: GridConfig handles this correctly — GridConfig.load() calls startConfigWatchers() on every load (GridConfig.swift:333), stopping and reopening the fds (:607, :614-642). BFDManager.reload() (:110-120) does not re-arm.
confirmed.symptom: User edits ~/.config/thegrid/bfd.yaml; the first save after server start applies, but subsequent saves silently do nothing — new/changed hotkeys don't take effect until the server is restarted, with no error anywhere.
confirmed.fixDirection: Re-arm the watcher (cancel + reopen fd) inside the event handler on .rename/.delete, or call startConfigWatcher() from reload() like GridConfig does; log when open() fails.
confirmed.evidence: BFDManager.swift:163-165 'let fd = open(expandedPath, O_EVTONLY); guard fd >= 0 else { return }' (silent). :167-171 eventMask [.write, .delete, .rename, .extend]; handler :173-187 only schedules reload(); no watcher recreation anywhere. GridConfig.swift:333 startConfigWatchers() invoked from load() on every reload, proving the codebase knows the re-arm pattern.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-read BFDManager.swift in full and re-traced every hop. (1) startConfigWatcher (BFDManager.swift:162-194) opens the fd exactly once (:164) and :165 'guard fd >= 0 else { return }' bails silently with no log, as claimed. (2) The event handler (:173-187) only debounces and schedules reload(); the cancel handler (:189-191) just closes the fd; there is no cancel+reopen anywhere. (3) grep confirms startConfigWatcher() is invoked only from start() (:64), and reload() (:110-120) only reloads BFDConfig — it never touches configWatcher, so nothing ever re-arms after a .rename/.delete fires. (4) The mechanism is sound macOS behavior: DispatchSource.makeFileSystemObjectSource is fd/vnode-based (kqueue), so after an atomic-rename save the fd tracks the dead inode and subsequent writes to the new file at the same path produce no events; the handler never re-resolves the path. No actor isolation, guard, or debounce breaks this — the debounce (:177-186) only coalesces events, it cannot resurrect a dead watch. (5) Contrast claim verified: GridConfig.load() (GridConfig.swift:263) ends with startConfigWatchers() (:333), reload() (:651) calls load() (:654), and startConfigWatchers() (:606-612) does stopConfigWatchers() then reopens both fds via startWatcher (:614-642) — the codebase demonstrably knows the re-arm pattern and BFD lacks it. (6) git log shows the file last changed in eb6a108; cited line numbers match current HEAD exactly. Only caveat: the symptom manifests only with atomic-rename-saving editors/tools; in-place writes keep working — a frequency qualifier, not a refutation, so severity stays medium.

GridConfig.startConfigWatchers() (GridConfig.swift:608-611) watches both config.yaml and config.local.yaml, confirming the asymmetry is an omission, not a design choice.

confirmed.title: BFDExecutor pipe-buffer deadlock: waitUntilExit before reading stdout/stderr
confirmed.mechanism: BFDExecutor.execute (BFDExecutor.swift:30-64) wires stdout/stderr to Pipes (:25-28), then calls 'process.waitUntilExit()' at :46 BEFORE reading the pipes at :49-50. If the hotkey command writes more than the ~64KB pipe buffer, the child blocks on write while the parent blocks in waitUntilExit — a classic deadlock. The 30s timeout work item (:34-44) then process.terminate()s the command mid-run and logs 'Command timed out after 30s', so a valid verbose command is killed and reported as a timeout. The codebase documents this exact hazard in the picker's subprocess helper — EnrichmentTypes.swift:52-56: 'Read pipe BEFORE waitUntilExit to avoid deadlock...' — but BFDExecutor does the opposite. executeAsync runs on a concurrent global queue, so other hotkeys still work, but each affected invocation burns a thread for 30s.
confirmed.symptom: A hotkey bound to a command with verbose output appears to hang, then is killed after 30 seconds with a 'timed out' bfd.error; the command's effect is partial (terminated mid-run) even though the command itself was fine.
confirmed.fixDirection: Read both pipes (readabilityHandler or readDataToEndOfFile on a background thread) before/concurrently with waitUntilExit, mirroring EnrichmentTypes.runProcess.
confirmed.evidence: BFDExecutor.swift:46-50: 'process.waitUntilExit()' then 'let stdoutData = stdoutPipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()'. EnrichmentTypes.swift:52-57 comment + correct ordering: 'let data = pipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile(); process.waitUntilExit()'.

confirmed.title: Terminal show() proceeds after AX failure, leaving a focused, opacity-1 window stranded off-screen (and can persist the off-screen frame)
confirmed.mechanism: hide() parks the Ghostty window at (-10000,-10000) with opacity 0 (GridTerminalManager.swift:181-186). show() is supposed to restore the frame first: :220-222 'if let element = windowManipulator.getAXElement(pid: pid, windowID: wid) { _ = windowManipulator.setWindowFrame(element: element, frame: targetFrame) }'. Both failure modes are ignored: getAXElement returning nil skips the reposition entirely; a false return from setWindowFrame is discarded via '_ ='. Either way, show() continues unconditionally: sets opacity to 1.0 (:225), orders the window to front (:228), AX-focuses it (:229), and sets isHidden = false (:231). Result: an invisible (off-screen but fully opaque) window now holds keyboard focus, swallowing all keystrokes. State says the terminal is shown, so the next toggle runs hide() — which at :174-177 reads the CURRENT frame (the off-screen position) from StateManager and persists it via saveFrame to terminal-frames.json, permanently poisoning the saved frame for that display so every future show() restores to off-screen.
confirmed.symptom: Terminal hotkey 'shows' the terminal but nothing appears; keystrokes go to an invisible window; in the persistence-poisoning variant the terminal never appears again on that display even across restarts, until terminal-frames.json is deleted.
confirmed.fixDirection: In show(), treat getAXElement-nil / setWindowFrame-false as a hard failure: retry or abort without flipping isHidden/opacity/focus; in hide(), refuse to save a frame whose origin is at/near the off-screen sentinel.
confirmed.evidence: GridTerminalManager.swift:220-222 'if let element = windowManipulator.getAXElement(pid: pid, windowID: wid) { _ = windowManipulator.setWindowFrame(element: element, frame: targetFrame) }' then :225 opacity 1.0, :229 focusWindow, :231 isHidden = false. hide() at :174-177 saves getCurrentFrame(wid:) unconditionally; :185 moves to Self.offScreenPoint = (-10000,-10000) (:57).

PRIMARY MECHANISM CONFIRMED: show() at GridTerminalManager.swift:220-222 skips the reposition when getAXElement returns nil and discards setWindowFrame's Bool via '_ ='; it then unconditionally sets opacity 1.0 (:225), orders front (:228), AX-focuses (:229), and sets isHidden=false (:231). getAXElement really can return nil (WindowManipulator.swift:64-66 windows-list copy failure, :82-84 WID-not-found with multiple windows; both log 'ax.fail', matching the logSignature) and setWindowPosition/setWindowFrame really can return false (WindowManipulator.swift:103-106, 139-155). hide() really parks at (-10000,-10000) opacity 0 (GridTerminalManager.swift:181-186, sentinel :57). No guard, debounce, or actor-isolation effect breaks this path — it is straight-line code inside one actor method. ESCALATION HOP REFUTED: the claim that the next hide() persists the off-screen frame to terminal-frames.json is wrong. hide() (:174-177) only calls saveFrame when getDisplayUUID(forWindow:) is non-nil; every StateManager path that writes a window frame recomputes displayUUID geometrically in the same operation (handleWindowMoved StateManager.swift:1561-1572, handleWindowResized :1574-1585, setWindowFrame :834-843, updateWindowFromPoll :1341-1372) via computeDisplayUUID (:935-940) → displayForWindowFrame (:895-899), which is center-point-in-display containment and returns nil for a frame at (-10000,-10000). The 'never appears again across restarts' symptom cannot occur. Also missed mitigation: getAXElement's single-AX-window fallback (WindowManipulator.swift:76-80) makes the nil path rarer for single-window Ghostty. confirmed.title: AX observer registration failure (-25204) at app launch is never retried — app runs unobserved
confirmed.mechanism: handleApplicationLaunched (StateManager.swift:1934) calls createObserver immediately on the NSWorkspace launch notification (:1945). createObserver fires 'Task { @MainActor in if observer.observe(stateManager: self) { await self.addApplicationObserver(...) } }' (:1202-1206) — when observe() returns false, the result is silently discarded; no retry timer, no backoff. observe() returns false when AXObserverAddNotification fails for all 8 notifications (ApplicationObserver.swift:85-93 'guard successCount > 0 else { ... return false }'), which is exactly what happens with kAXErrorCannotComplete (-25204) when a freshly launched app's AX server isn't up yet. createObserver is only re-invoked at server startup (:131), the next launch of the same app (:1945), or a post-wake rebuildAXObservers (:2095) — so an app that loses this launch race gets NO AXCreated/Destroyed/FocusedWindowChanged/Moved/Resized events for its entire lifetime; it is covered only by the 3s poll and the 300ms focus sweep.
confirmed.symptom: For the affected app: new windows take up to 3s to tile (poll latency), window destroys leave stale cell entries until the next poll/validator pass, and per-window move/resize tracking is absent — intermittent, app-specific sluggish/incorrect tiling that disappears after a server restart or sleep/wake.
confirmed.fixDirection: On observe() failure, schedule bounded retries with delay (e.g. 0.5s/1s/2s) before giving up, and include pid/app in the failure log.

confirmed.title: not_standard creation bail is terminal — a window misclassified as floating at creation never gets re-evaluated
confirmed.mechanism: handleWindowCreated classifies the window after the isTileable gate (GridReconciler.swift:602-611). classifyWindow returns .floating for an AXStandardWindow with no fullscreen button (GridAssignment.swift:94); hasFullscreenButton comes from a one-shot AX query at creation (StateManager.swift:1483-1491) — apps that populate window buttons slightly after creating the AX element read as button-less. Unlike the not_tileable path (:589 rejectWindow), the not_standard bail does NOT reject the window, so neither rejectedWindowSweep (:388) nor handleWindowMoved's unreject path (:1025) ever re-evaluates it, and StateManager's nil-role re-query (StateManager.swift:1355-1367) doesn't apply because role is already non-nil. The window floats permanently. The only recovery is a manual layout apply — and GridApply.filterTileableFromState doesn't consult classifyWindow at all (GridApply.swift:546), which is itself an inconsistency: applyLayout adopts no-fullscreen-button windows into cells that the live reconciler refuses.
confirmed.symptom: A slow-starting app's main window occasionally floats untiled despite being a normal standard window; the same window DOES get tiled if the user reapplies the layout, confirming the classification disagreement between the create path and the apply path.
confirmed.fixDirection: Track not_standard bails for a short grace period and re-classify on the next move/resize or sweep tick; also reconcile classifyWindow (create path) with the apply path so both agree.
confirmed.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:603-611: 'let category = classifyWindow(...); if category != .standard { jlog("reconcile.win.create.bail", ... "reason": "not_standard" ...); return }' — no rejectWindow call, contrast with :589. GridAssignment.swift:93-96: '// PIP detection: no fullscreen button AND not a known terminal app\n if !window.hasFullscreenButton && !terminalApps.contains(appName) { return .floating }'.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop. (1) GridReconciler.swift:602-612: not_standard bail logs and returns with no rejectWindow call, unlike the not_tileable path at :589 — read directly. (2) GridAssignment.swift:89-96: AXStandardWindow with !hasFullscreenButton and non-terminal app returns .floating (PIP heuristic). (3) StateManager.swift:1483-1491: hasFullscreenButton set from a single getAXProperties call in handleWindowCreated; the only later re-queries for an existing window are gated on role == nil (StateManager.swift:1355-1367 poll path, :992 space-change path), and the full re-query refreshWindows (:1090) runs only from refreshCompleteState, called solely at startup (StateManager.swift:117) and system wake (:2069). So a non-nil-role window's stale hasFullscreenButton=false persists indefinitely. (4) GridReconciler.swift:384-409: rejectedWindowSweep iterates only gridState.getRejectedWindows() — never sees the not_standard window. (5) GridReconciler.swift:1025: handleWindowMoved recovery guarded by isWindowRejected, so it returns early for this window. (6) StateManager.swift:1272-1300: poll emits windowCreated only for newly discovered windows; updateWindowFromPoll emits no events. Therefore the not_standard bail is terminal and the window floats permanently — the core mechanism is confirmed end-to-end. One sub-claim in the finding is wrong, in the direction that strengthens the bug: the alleged apply-path inconsistency does not exist. filterTileableFromState (GridApply.swift:528-559, called at :159) indeed skips classifyWindow, but its output feeds GridAssignment.assignWindows (GridApply.swift:171), which calls shouldFloat -> classifyWindow at GridAssignment.swift:277/:174 and routes the no-fullscreen-button window into result.floating, never into a cell. So manual layout reapply does NOT recover the window (it re-classifies from the same stale state); the claimed symptom 'tiles on reapply' is contradicted by code. Actual recovery requires system wake or server restart (refreshCompleteState -> refreshWindows re-reads AX buttons, wake then runs refreshAllDisplays per GridReconciler.swift:998). Git log shows no relevant changes since the finding (last GridReconciler.swift commit 713cf7a); commit 1cf354e (phantom promotion) only touched the nil-role fallback in getAXProperties, irrelevant here. The single unverifiable hop is empirical, not code: whether real apps populate AX window buttons after the create notification (plausible AX race, cannot be proven from the repo). confirmed.title: Fire-and-forget dead-window prune races setFocus, recording a dead/wrong lastFocusedWid
confirmed.mechanism: cycleFocus (GridFocus.swift:228-234) and focusCellByID (:318-323) prune dead windows from a LOCAL copy of the cell list but remove them from GridState via detached 'Task { await gridState.removeWindow(...) }' (:230 and :320) with no ordering relative to the subsequent 'await gridState.setFocus(spaceID:cellID:windowIndex:)' (:243/:263/:362). The windowIndex is computed against the filtered local array, but if setFocus reaches the GridState actor before the prune Task, GridState.setFocus (GridState.swift:640-659) resolves 'newWID = cell.windows[windowIndex]' (:647-648) against the UNpruned array — recording the dead window (or the wrong neighbor) as cell.lastFocusedWid and space.focusedWindow. focusCellByID's restore priority uses lastFocusedWid first (:336-348), so the next entry into that cell can raise the wrong window. The state partially self-heals when removeWindow later runs (GridState.swift:397-408 resets lastFocusedWid==dead to prevFocusedWid), but the wrong-neighbor case persists.
confirmed.symptom: Right after a window in a cell closes, focusing or cycling into that cell raises a different window than the one last used.
confirmed.fixDirection: Await the removeWindow calls (they are already in an async context) instead of detaching them, so setFocus indexes the pruned state.
confirmed.evidence: GridFocus.swift:228-231 'cellWindows = cellWindows.filter { wid in if wmState.windows[String(wid)] != nil { return true }; Task { await gridState.removeWindow(wid, fromSpace: spaceID) } ...'; GridState.swift:647-648 'if windowIndex >= 0 && windowIndex < cell.windows.count { let newWID = cell.windows[windowIndex]'. confirmed.title: DispatchQueue.main.sync from inside the StateManager actor (removeObserver)
confirmed.mechanism: removeObserver (StateManager.swift:1217-1230) executes 'DispatchQueue.main.sync { observer.stopObserving() }' while running on the StateManager actor's cooperative-pool thread. It is called from handleApplicationTerminated (:1965, on every app quit) and shutdown (:175). Blocking a cooperative-pool thread on the main queue violates Swift concurrency's forward-progress contract: the actor is stalled for as long as the main thread is busy (border pool rebuilds, picker rendering, AX callbacks), and every event/command awaiting StateManager queues behind it. It becomes a hard deadlock if the main thread ever synchronously waits on StateManager (none today, but rebuildAXObservers at :2086-2091 shows the safe await MainActor.run pattern this code should use).
confirmed.symptom: Brief whole-server stalls when apps quit while the main thread is busy; latent deadlock if any future main-thread code blocks on the actor.
confirmed.fixDirection: Make removeObserver async and use await MainActor.run { observer.stopObserving() } like rebuildAXObservers does.
confirmed.evidence: StateManager.swift:1220-1224 '// Stop observing FIRST (synchronously on main thread) ... DispatchQueue.main.sync { observer.stopObserving() }' inside actor-isolated method; contrast :2088-2090 'await MainActor.run { observer.stopObserving() }'.

confirmed.title: GridState.load() races startup event handling and clobbers in-memory mutations
confirmed.mechanism: main.swift:140-143 creates GridState and spawns an unordered 'Task { await gridState.load() }' while a sibling Task (main.swift:160+) starts StateManager and wires GridReconciler. Nothing sequences load() before the reconciler registers with EventRouter (GridReconciler.swift:304-306) or before commands can arrive. GridState.load (GridState.swift:113-124) wholesale replaces 'spaces = decoded.spaces' — any assignment/migration GridState performed between server start and load completion (e.g. a windowCreated handled by the reconciler in the first hundreds of ms, or an early CLI layout apply) is silently discarded when the decode finishes.

confirmed.title: SocketServer.sendMessage called concurrently per socket — JSONL frames can interleave
confirmed.mechanism: sendMessage (SocketServer.swift:233-254) writes 'data + \n' with a single send() call but is invoked from multiple concurrent contexts for the same client socket with no per-socket serialization: (a) request responses arrive via MessageHandler completion inside per-request Tasks (SocketServer.swift:227-229, MessageHandler.swift:52); (b) EventBroadcaster.broadcast iterates ALL clientSockets (EventBroadcaster.swift:32-39) and calls server.sendMessage from whatever context fired the event. A client awaiting a response while events are broadcast can receive two send() calls racing on the same fd; for large messages (state dumps exceed the socket buffer) send() can partially write, interleaving bytes of two JSON lines and corrupting the newline-delimited framing for that client.
confirmed.symptom: CLI/viewer occasionally receives unparseable JSON or a response glued to an event line, surfacing as client-side parse errors or timed-out commands under event-heavy load.
confirmed.fixDirection: Funnel all writes for a given client socket through a per-socket serial queue (or the existing socketQueue).
confirmed.evidence: SocketServer.swift:240-242 'let sent = data.withUnsafeBytes { ptr in send(socket, ptr.baseAddress, data.count, 0) }' with callers at :227-229 (response path, concurrent Tasks) and EventBroadcaster.swift:34-39 (broadcast loop, unsynchronized).
confirmed.logSignature: "ev":"msg.err".*"op":"parse" on the client side / sock.err op send

Every hop holds at current HEAD: (1) sendMessage (SocketServer.swift:233-254) is on a plain class — no actor, no lock — and does a single unsynchronized send() at :240-242; (2) response path is concurrent: handleRequest :227-229 → MessageHandler.swift:52 spawns an unstructured Task per request whose completion calls sendMessage, and clients are serviced on clientQueue declared `.concurrent` (SocketServer.swift:10); (3) EventBroadcaster.broadcast (EventBroadcaster.swift:32-39) snapshots sockets via getClientSockets() then calls sendMessage OUTSIDE any queue, fired from ResizeManager's own serial queue (ResizeManager.swift:20,133,180,209), the heartbeat timerQueue, and the concurrent clientQueue via the relay at SocketServer.swift:194; (4) the only serial queue (socketQueue, line 11) protects the clientSockets set and SocketServer.broadcast(:257-263) only — neither the response path nor EventBroadcaster goes through it, so it does not refute the race; (5) git log shows the file last changed in 906deba, line numbers in the finding match exactly. confirmed.title: assignAutoFlow silently drops every window when all cells are locked
confirmed.mechanism: GridAssignment.assignAutoFlow filters locked cells out of the candidate list (GridAssignment.swift:370 'sortedCells = sortedCells.filter { !lockedCells.contains($0) }') and then bails with 'guard !sortedCells.isEmpty else { return }' (:372) — no log, no error. Any window in the batch that did not match a locked app rule simply never appears in result.assignments, so applyLayout (GridApply.swift:266 setWindowAssignments) commits an assignment map that omits those windows entirely: they are untracked, untiled, get no border, and cannot be focused/moved via grid commands. Trigger requires a layout where every cell carries a locked app rule (realistic for small 2-cell layouts with two locked apps), then opening any non-matching app and applying a layout. Suspected because no user config exercising an all-locked layout was verified.
confirmed.symptom: After applying a layout where all cells are locked to specific apps, windows of other apps are left floating wherever they were — no placement, no border, no log explaining why.
confirmed.fixDirection: Log a warn (e.g. assign.dropped with wids) when the filtered cell list is empty, and/or fall back to assigning to the least-populated locked cell rather than dropping windows.

(1) GridAssignment.swift:370-372 contains the exact quoted filter + 'guard !sortedCells.isEmpty else { return }' with no logging anywhere in assignAutoFlow; dropped windows are never added to result.assignments, result.floating, or result.excluded. (2) GridApply.swift:254+266 commits assignment.assignments verbatim via setWindowAssignments, and GridState.swift:592-600 sets space.cells = [:] before rebuilding from the map, so any prior tracking of the dropped windows is erased. (3) No rescue path exists: sweepDisplacedWindows (GridReconciler.swift:1394-1437) iterates only gridState.getAllWindowIDs() so untracked windows are invisible to it; the new-window path's pickTargetCell (GridReconciler.swift:1367-1382) returns "" when all assignment cells are in the locked set, and the 'if !targetCell.isEmpty' guard at :687 silently skips assignment — the same silent-drop behavior. (4) git log shows the file last changed in 140a7ed/eb6a108, predating the audit; cited lines match current code. Hunted for refutations and found none: no actor isolation, debounce, or guard breaks the path. Trigger nuances cut both ways: lockedCellIDs (GridAssignment.swift:217-225) is layout-agnostic, so locked rules naming generic cell IDs (left/right) poison every layout sharing those IDs, making the all-locked precondition easier to hit than the finder thought; but autoFlow is not a default strategy (applyLayout defaults to .position at GridApply.swift:79, reapplyLayout to .preserve at :280), so it requires an explicit 'autoflow' strategy request (GridCommandRouter.swift:956). Net: mechanism fully confirmed, low severity stands.

confirmed.title: Nudge double-enter leaks a live CGEventTap and permanently suppresses the reconciler
confirmed.mechanism: Each '@nudge enter' request runs in its own unstructured Task (BFDManager.swift:137 for hotkeys, MessageHandler.swift:52 for socket requests) against the plain non-actor GridCommandRouter. handleNudge's idempotency check `if nudgeKeyHandler != nil` (GridCommandRouter.swift:779) is followed by a suspension point `await resolveActiveSpaceID()` (GridCommandRouter.swift:785) before the handler is finally stored at GridCommandRouter.swift:830. A second concurrent enter (double-tap of the hotkey before BFD is suspended at line 793) passes the nil check during the first task's await. Both tasks then: (a) call gridReconciler.beginAction (GridCommandRouter.swift:790), which is a bare counter increment with no token identity (GridReconciler.swift:134-137, ActionToken is just label+timestamp); (b) create and start two NudgeKeyHandlers (GridCommandRouter.swift:796, 824) — two live CGEventTaps that each consume hjkl/arrows/escape and fire onNudge (NudgeKeyHandler.swift:137-194 returns nil to consume); (c) both assign nudgeKeyHandler at line 830 — the losing handler is orphaned with stop() never called. On '@nudge exit' (GridCommandRouter.swift:841-866) only the stored handler is stopped (848-849) and endAction is called once (861) — suppressionDepth stays >= 1 forever (GridReconciler.swift:146 max(0, depth-1)), so suppressReconciliation is permanently true and (per the existing GridReconciler.swift:442 behavior) all windowCreated/windowDestroyed events are silently dropped from then on. Meanwhile the orphaned tap keeps consuming hjkl/arrow keys system-wide and keeps moving/resizing windows via gridNudge on every keypress, even though BFD was resumed and nudge mode is 'exited'. Separately, two concurrent '@nudge exit' tasks on different threads can both pass the guard at 843 and both read the non-nil nudgeActionToken before either nils it at 863, calling endAction twice and stripping another session's suppression (logged as warn.action.end.underflow only when depth is already 0). nudgeKeyHandler/nudgeActionToken are also plain stored properties on a non-Sendable class mutated from arbitrary executor threads — an outright data race.
confirmed.symptom: After double-tapping the nudge hotkey and later exiting nudge mode: hjkl/arrow keys stop reaching apps and instead keep moving/resizing the focused window forever (until server restart); window manager stops tiling new windows and never removes closed ones (reconciler permanently suppressed).
confirmed.fixDirection: Make nudge session state actor-isolated (or route handleNudge through a serial queue); give ActionToken a unique id and make endAction consume it exactly once; stop-and-replace any existing handler before installing a new one.
confirmed.evidence: GridCommandRouter.swift:779 `if nudgeKeyHandler != nil { return .ok("already in nudge mode") }` ... :785 `guard let spaceID = await resolveActiveSpaceID()` (suspension before) ... :790 `let token = gridReconciler.beginAction(label: "nudge")` ... :830 `nudgeKeyHandler = handler`. GridReconciler.swift:134-137 `func beginAction(label:) -> ActionToken { suppressionDepth += 1 ... return ActionToken(label:..., startTime:...) }` — token carries no identity, endAction (142-146) blindly decrements. Exit path :843 `guard nudgeKeyHandler != nil else`, :861 `gridReconciler.endAction(token, syncBorders: true)`. NudgeKeyHandler consumes keys: NudgeKeyHandler.swift:137 'Returns nil to consume the event', :190-194. Logs: zero '"ev":"nudge.enter"' entries to date (feature unused in production so far), 0 underflow warnings.
lenses: round2:Command ingress concurrency: MessageHandler + GridCommandRouter (3,000 untouched LOC at the entry point of every command)

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop. (1) GridCommandRouter.swift:32 is a plain class; nudgeKeyHandler/nudgeActionToken are unsynchronized stored properties (:50,:54). (2) Both ingress points spawn unstructured Tasks on the global executor: BFDManager.swift handleInternalCommand (Task { await router.dispatch }) and MessageHandler.swift dispatchAndRespond (~:1390). (3) dispatch routes nudge directly to handleNudge with no executeAction wrapper (GridCommandRouter.swift:199-202). (4) The idempotency check at :779 is separated from the store at :830 by a real suspension (await resolveActiveSpaceID -> await stateManager.getState(), :785/:306), so two concurrent enters both pass the nil check. (5) GridReconciler.swift:74-77,134-157: ActionToken is label+startTime only; beginAction bare-increments suppressionDepth, endAction blindly decrements. (6) Exit (:843-862) stops only the stored handler and ends only the stored token once; a second exit no-ops at :843's guard — depth stuck at 1 permanently. (7) GridReconciler.swift:442 drops windowCreated/windowDestroyed while suppressed — reconciler permanently dead until restart. Git log on the file shows no changes since 713cf7a; cited lines match. HOWEVER one headline sub-claim is wrong: the 'orphaned live CGEventTap keeps consuming hjkl forever' part is refuted by NudgeKeyHandler.swift:67-70 deinit { stop() } combined with Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) at :91 — nothing retains the losing handler (run-loop source retains only the CFMachPort; onNudge captures router weakly), so it deallocates when the losing task returns and deinit tears the tap down within milliseconds. The 'keys hijacked until server restart' symptom cannot occur. The double-exit race (:843) is technically possible but has no suspension point between guard (:843) and nil-out (:849), so it needs same-instant parallelism — much narrower than claimed. BFD suspend/resume imbalance is harmless (boolean-guarded, BFDKeyHandler.swift:161-172). Net: the core mechanism (double-enter leaks suppressionDepth, permanently suppressing the reconciler) is fully confirmed in code; the keyboard-hijack half of the symptom is refuted, which removes the worst user-facing impact and justifies a severity downgrade from critical to high. Note logs show zero nudge.enter events to date and the enter race window is the duration of one stateManager.getState() await.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: NudgeKeyHandler.swift:67-70 `deinit { Safety net: release OS resources if caller forgot to call stop(); stop() }` and :91 `userInfo: Unmanaged.passUnretained(self).toOpaque()` — the tap does not retain the handler, so the overwritten handler deallocates and its deinit stops the tap (refutes the permanent key-consumption claim). BFDKeyHandler.swift:161-172: suspend()/resume() are boolean-guarded via CGEvent.tapIsEnabled, so double-suspend/single-resume from the double-enter does not leak BFD state. GridCommandRouter.swift:199-202 comment confirms nudge intentionally bypasses the executeAction wrapper. GridCommandRouter.swift:306 resolveActiveSpaceID awaits stateManager.getState() — a genuine suspension point making the enter race window real. Exit path has no suspension between guard (:843) and nil-out (:849), narrowing the claimed double-exit race to raw thread-level timing.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code evidence actively demonstrates every link in the claimed mechanism. (1) Re-read grid-server/Sources/GridServer/Grid/GridCommandRouter.swift:32 — plain `class GridCommandRouter`, and dispatch (line 158) has no serialization; it even awaits gridReconciler.awaitWakeCompletion() before routing, widening the race window. (2) handleNudge enter path verified at lines 774-839: nil idempotency check at 779, suspension `await resolveActiveSpaceID()` at 785, `beginAction(label: "nudge")` at 790, BFD tap suspended only after that, handler assigned at 830 — a genuine TOCTOU window during which a second concurrent enter passes the nil check, producing two started CGEventTaps where the loser is orphaned (stop() never called) and two suppressionDepth increments. (3) Concurrent ingress confirmed: MessageHandler.swift:52 spawns an unstructured `Task {}` per socket request; BFDManager.swift handleInternalCommand spawns `Task { await router.dispatch(command) }` per hotkey. (4) GridReconciler.swift:21 is a plain class; beginAction (134-137) is a bare counter returning a token with no identity, endAction (142-156) blindly decrements with max(0, depth-1); suppressReconciliation = depth>0 (line 58) and line 442-444 drops all window events while suppressed — so one leaked begin permanently suppresses the reconciler exactly as claimed. (5) BFD/NudgeKeyHandler.swift handleEvent returns nil to consume hjkl/arrows/escape, so an orphaned tap keeps eating those keys system-wide. Log check: grepped ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json (153,704 lines) — zero "ev":"nudge.enter", zero "label":"nudge", zero warn.action.end.underflow, and all 64 action.begin events are depth:1 (label picker.result). Logs neither contradict nor demonstrate the bug; they show the nudge feature has never been used in production. Minor citation nit: NudgeKeyHandler.swift lives under BFD/, not Grid/.

confirmed.title: Command ingress is fully unserialized: per-request/per-keypress unstructured Tasks run grid commands concurrently — log-confirmed 4-way overlap and lost resize increments
confirmed.mechanism: Every socket request spawns a bare `Task { ... handler(request) }` in MessageHandler.handle (MessageHandler.swift:52-84), and every BFD '@' hotkey — including auto-repeats at the 50ms rate limit — spawns its own `Task { await router.dispatch(command) }` in BFDManager.handleInternalCommand (BFDManager.swift:137). GridCommandRouter.dispatch (GridCommandRouter.swift:158) is an async method on a plain class with no queue, so N in-flight commands execute genuinely concurrently and complete in arbitrary order. Concrete lost-update path: holding the resize hotkey emits '@resize grow 0.01' every 50ms; each dispatch runs handleResize (GridCommandRouter.swift:513-533) -> GridResize.adjustFocusedSplit, which snapshots splitRatios via getSpaceReadOnly (GridResize.swift:64, :86), computes new ratios, and writes them back at GridResize.swift:107 before reapplyLayout (:113). Two concurrent tasks both read ratio R and both write R+0.01 — one increment lost — and their reapplyLayout passes interleave AX window placements. Production logs show this trigger and the overlap: 492 same-second bursts of bfd.internal commands (e.g. five '@resize grow 0.01' in one second) and 11 instances of a second action.start arriving before the prior action.end, peaking at 4 concurrent focus.* executeAction sessions. This caller-side absence of ordering is what creates every downstream race already filed against GridReconciler/GridFocus; nothing at the ingress layer serializes commands per window, per space, or globally.
confirmed.symptom: Held-key resize grows/shrinks less than the number of keypresses and windows visibly stutter to wrong intermediate sizes; rapid focus-hotkey repeats land on the wrong window or ping-pong; interleaved move/apply commands place windows from a half-applied earlier command.
confirmed.fixDirection: Funnel GridCommandRouter.dispatch through a single serial executor (make the router an actor, or an AsyncStream command queue consumed by one task), coalescing repeat-key commands.
confirmed.evidence: MessageHandler.swift:52 `Task { await CurrentSpan.$current.withValue(span) { ... handler(request) ... } }` — one detached task per request. BFDManager.swift:137-138 `Task { let result = await router.dispatch(command) }` — one per hotkey repeat. GridResize.swift:86 `var ratios = cell.splitRatios` (snapshot) ... :107 `await gridState.setCellSplitRatios(...)` (blind write). Log analysis (thegrid-server.json): 492 same-second bfd.internal bursts incl. 5x '@resize grow 0.01' at ts 1780522359; action.start/action.end pairing shows 11 overlaps, max 4 concurrent (e.g. 'focus.left' starting at depth 2 at ts 1780459359).
confirmed.logSignature: two "ev":"action.start" lines with no intervening "ev":"action.end"; bursts of "ev":"bfd.internal" with identical ts
lenses: round2:Command ingress concurrency: MessageHandler + GridCommandRouter (3,000 untouched LOC at the entry point of every command)

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop in code and re-ran the log analysis from scratch; all hold. (1) Ingress: grid-server/Sources/GridServer/MessageHandler.swift:52-84 spawns a bare `Task { await CurrentSpan.$current.withValue(span) { ... handler(request) ... } }` per request; MessageHandler is a plain class and `handle` is nonisolated, so the Task inherits no actor and runs on the global concurrent executor. (2) Hotkey ingress: grid-server/Sources/GridServer/BFD/BFDManager.swift:136-142 spawns `Task { let result = await router.dispatch(command) }` per '@' hotkey; BFDManager is `class BFDManager: NSObject` (line 5), no debounce or coalescing in handleInternalCommand. (3) Router: grid-server/Sources/GridServer/Grid/GridCommandRouter.swift:32 `class GridCommandRouter` (not an actor), dispatch at :158; the only gate is `gridReconciler.awaitWakeCompletion()` which handles sleep/wake only and is a no-op fast path — no lock/semaphore/in-flight guard anywhere in the file. (4) I hunted for serializers the finder might have missed: GridReconciler.executeAction (GridReconciler.swift:91-129) uses a reentrant `suppressionDepth += 1` counter that explicitly supports overlap (and GridReconciler is a plain class at line 21, so the counter itself is unsynchronized); resize commands don't even route through executeAction (GridCommandRouter.swift:513-540 calls gridResize.adjustFocusedSplit directly). (5) Lost-update: GridResize.swift adjustFocusedSplit snapshots via `await gridState.getSpaceReadOnly(spaceID)`, computes from stale `cell.splitRatios`, blind-writes via `await gridState.setCellSplitRatios(...)`, then `reapplyLayout` — GridState IS an actor (GridState.swift:84), but the read and write are separate actor hops separated by suspension points, so two concurrent dispatches both reading ratio R and writing R+0.01 is exactly the classic actor-reentrancy lost update; actor isolation does not refute it. (6) Independently re-parsed ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json with my own script: 11 overlapping action.start events (depth>1) with max concurrent depth 4 — exact match to the finding; 432 distinct seconds with multiple bfd.internal events, max 12 in one second (finding's 492 likely counts events rather than seconds; the burst phenomenon is confirmed regardless). (7) git log -8 on MessageHandler.swift shows no commit altering this mechanism; line 52 contains exactly the cited code today.

GridCommandRouter.swift:158-167: dispatch's only gate is `await gridReconciler.awaitWakeCompletion()` — wake-validation only, nil fast path, not a serializer. GridReconciler.swift:21 `class GridReconciler: StateEventHandler` and :99 `suppressionDepth += 1` — reentrant counter on a non-actor class, supports overlap by design (matches log max depth 4). evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code evidence fully confirms the unserialized-ingress mechanism: MessageHandler.swift:52 spawns a bare Task per socket request; BFD/BFDManager.swift:137-142 spawns a Task per hotkey (incl. 50ms auto-repeats); GridCommandRouter.swift:32 is a plain class and dispatch (:158) has no serialization beyond awaitWakeCompletion; GridResize.swift:86-117 is a textbook read-modify-write across awaits (snapshot splitRatios, blind setCellSplitRatios). Log evidence confirms real concurrent execution: pairing action.start with action.end/action.err correctly (executeAction emits action.err on throw; endAction's action.end carries dur_ms and pairs with action.begin; resetting at srv.start), I reproduce the finding's exact numbers — 11 overlapping executeAction sessions, max 4 concurrent, including focus.left at ts 1780459359 at depth 2 (GridReconciler.swift:96/:114 emit sites verified). 432 same-second bfd.internal bursts also verified (finding said 492; same order of magnitude). HOWEVER, the headline concrete symptom — lost resize increments — is contradicted by the logs: in every resize burst, including 12x '@resize grow 0.01' in one second at ts 1780736053, the sequence cmd.dispatch → action.start → action.end → resize.split.done strictly alternates with zero interleaving; each resize completes faster than the 50ms key-repeat interval, so resizes ran serially in practice and no lost update is demonstrated in 153,715 log lines. The genuine overlaps (11 of ~2,093 actions, ~0.5%, mostly depth 2; the depth-4 peak is layout.apply at ts 1781067003, not focus.* as the finding states) show the race window is real but rare. Verdict: confirmed (mechanism actively demonstrated in code and logs), but severity should come down from high since the most concrete lost-update path never manifests and observed overlap frequency is low.
evidenceVerdict.addedEvidence: Corrected log pairing analysis (action.err on throws at GridReconciler.swift:130; endAction action.end distinguished by dur_ms at GridReconciler.swift:147): 11 overlaps / max depth 4, matching the finding. Contradicting evidence for the resize lost-update: heaviest burst ts 1780736052-54 (21 consecutive '@resize grow 0.01') shows perfectly serial {cmd.dispatch → action.start(layout.apply) → action.end → resize.split.done} alternation — no overlap; same for the ts 1780522358-62 burst. Apparent resize 'in-flight 81' was an artifact of error-path dispatches (cmd.err 'atEdgeOfLayout' at ts 1780801690 emits no resize.*.done). confirmed.title: All @notify actions collapse to launch-or-toggle: handleNotify ignores action and args, and buildCommand drops notify payload params
confirmed.mechanism: MessageHandler registers ten notify RPCs (grid.notify.show/hide/toggle/push/list/dismiss/clear/count/assign/unassign, MessageHandler.swift:1907-1962) that build command strings like '@notify push ...' and dispatch through the router. dispatch routes the whole 'notify' domain to handleNotify (GridCommandRouter.swift:197-198), but handleNotify (GridCommandRouter.swift:880-930) never reads cmd.action or cmd.args: it only checks whether GridNotify.app is running, launches it if not (:885-919), or posts the same 'com.thegrid.notify.toggle' distributed notification regardless of action (:923-929). So 'grid.notify.hide' SHOWS the panel when it is hidden, 'grid.notify.show' hides it when visible, and push/list/dismiss/clear/count/assign/unassign all just toggle panel visibility. Compounding: buildCommand (MessageHandler.swift:1407-1472) has no handling for title/body/priority/source/id/purge params, so even if handleNotify parsed actions, grid.notify.push's payload is silently discarded before dispatch. (buildCommand also appends --strategy/--space/--display twice — once in the valueFlags loop at :1447-1455 and again at :1457-1469 — currently harmless duplication.)
confirmed.symptom: Any client calling notify RPCs gets wrong-direction behavior: hide shows the panel, push/dismiss/clear toggle visibility instead of acting, and notification payloads vanish — all while the RPC returns ok:true ('toggled').

confirmed.title: MessageHandler.handlers dictionary is written after the socket starts accepting — unsynchronized Dictionary race and a startup window where all grid.* methods 404
confirmed.mechanism: MessageHandler is a plain class with `private var handlers: [String: RequestHandler]` (MessageHandler.swift:15). register() mutates it with no lock (MessageHandler.swift:26). main.swift starts the socket server at main.swift:122 (`try socketServer.start()`), but registerGridHandlers — ~40 more register() calls on the main thread — only runs at main.swift:229. SocketServer accepts connections on a concurrent clientQueue (SocketServer.swift:10, :133) and handleRequest calls handler.handle (SocketServer.swift:227), whose Task reads `handlers[request.method]` on a cooperative-pool thread (MessageHandler.swift:56). A request arriving in the start-to-registration window produces a concurrent Dictionary read while the main thread inserts — undefined behavior in Swift (possible crash/corruption) — and, benignly, any grid.* request in that window gets -32601 'Method not found'. Realistic trigger: server restart (launchd / make run) while BFD-spawned CLI processes or a retry loop are hammering the socket. Disproof attempt: no synchronization or ordering barrier exists anywhere between start() and registerGridHandlers; the only mitigation is the small (~tens of ms) window, hence 'suspected' — production logs currently show 0 method_not_found hits.
confirmed.symptom: Rare crash at startup, or first hotkey/CLI command after a server restart fails with 'Method not found: grid.focus' despite the server being up.
confirmed.fixDirection: Register all handlers (or at least construct MessageHandler fully) before socketServer.start(), or guard the handlers map with a lock/actor.

confirmed.title: Nudge keystrokes spawn unordered Tasks doing read-modify-write on the cached frame — held arrow key loses steps
confirmed.mechanism: NudgeKeyHandler.onNudge fires synchronously on the main thread per keypress, and the router callback bridges each one into an independent unstructured `Task { ... gridNudge.move(...) }` (GridCommandRouter.swift:803-813) with no ordering or coalescing. GridNudge.move (GridNudge.swift:67-104) is a read-modify-write against cached state: ManipulationContext.from reads the frame from StateManager's cached snapshot (WindowManipulator.swift:29-38, `frame: windowState.frame`), computes newOrigin = currentFrame.origin ± 20 (GridNudge.swift:82-95), then performs the AX move; the cache is only updated after the AX call succeeds (WindowManipulator.swift:165-168). Key auto-repeat (~30-60ms) is faster than the AX round-trip, so consecutive keypress Tasks read the same stale frame, compute the same target origin, and N presses collapse into 1 step; out-of-order completion can also leave the window at an earlier target. The session also pins spaceID at enter time (GridCommandRouter.swift:785, comment at 783-784), so if the user switches spaces mid-session, nudges keep moving the focused window of the old space.
confirmed.symptom: Holding an arrow/hjkl key in nudge mode moves the window far fewer steps than keypresses (or it jumps backward), with border overlay desyncing from the window.
confirmed.fixDirection: Serialize nudge actions through one queue/AsyncStream per session and carry the frame forward between steps (or re-read the live AX frame) instead of the cached StateManager frame.

GridNudge.swift:78 `guard let context = await ManipulationContext.from(windowID: wid)`; :83 `let currentFrame = context.frame ?? .zero`; :88 `newOrigin = CGPoint(x: currentFrame.origin.x - step, ...)`. WindowManipulator.swift:30-37 builds context.frame from `state.windows[String(windowID)]?.frame` (cached), and :164-168 updates the cache only after setWindowPosition succeeds.

confirmed.title: Router-level stale-space TOCTOU: spaceID resolved once, then acted on across awaits — '@state reset' and resize/layout can hit the space the user just left
confirmed.mechanism: resolveActiveSpaceID (GridCommandRouter.swift:305-307) snapshots wmState and derives the active space, then every handler proceeds through further awaits using that string. With commands queuing behind concurrent dispatch Tasks (finding 2: up to 4 in-flight observed) plus the reconciler's awaitWakeCompletion gate at GridCommandRouter.swift:167, the gap between hotkey press and spaceID resolution-vs-action can span a user space switch. Concrete paths: handleState 'reset' (GridCommandRouter.swift:656-662) resolves spaceID then calls gridState.removeSpace(spaceID) — if a space switch landed in between (which per the existing StateManager.swift:1762 finding migrates/destroys GridState keyed by spaceID), the reset wipes the wrong space's grid state or a freshly-migrated one. handleResize (GridCommandRouter.swift:513-516) resolves spaceID before switching on action, then adjustFocusedSplit/reapplyLayout manipulate windows of that space — repositioning windows on a now-inactive space, which the displacement sweep then bounces (existing GridReconciler.swift:1426/660 findings). handleLayout apply/cycle (GridCommandRouter.swift:385-401) has the same shape. Marked suspected: each individual window is one or two awaits wide and I found no log instance proving a cross-space hit; but no guard exists anywhere re-validating the space before acting.
confirmed.symptom: Right after switching spaces, a queued reset/resize/layout hotkey silently mutates the previous space: its grid state is wiped or its windows get re-laid-out and later bounced by the sweep.
confirmed.fixDirection: Re-resolve (or verify) the active space immediately before the mutating call inside each handler, aborting with a 'space changed' error on mismatch.

confirmed.title: Wake unconditionally resumes StateValidator while screen is still locked, ax_orphan-pruning real windows
confirmed.mechanism: Lid close / lock fires screenLocked and systemWillSleep, both pausing the validator (GridReconciler.swift:456-460 -> StateValidator.pause() :97). On lid open, NSWorkspace.didWakeNotification routes .systemWoke; GridReconciler.handleSystemWake Step 0 'unconditionally resume the validator' (GridReconciler.swift:959-962) runs BEFORE the user has unlocked (com.apple.screenIsUnlocked has not fired). Step 1.5 resets all orphan counts (:985), then Step 2 runs validate() immediately (:990) and the 30s periodic timer (StateValidator.swift:137-158) keeps firing. At the lock screen, AX queries succeed but return reduced window lists — StateValidator's own comment (:94-96) says exactly this is why pause exists. pruneAXOrphanedWindows (StateValidator.swift:233-277) increments orphan counts: count=1 at wake validate (~t+2.5s, after StateManager's 2s stabilization sleep at StateManager.swift:2067), count=2 at the next 30s tick -> gridState.removeWindowFromAllSpaces(windowID) (:270). Any user who takes more than ~30s to type their password after opening the lid gets real windows pruned from GridState; on unlock they are untiled and their cell assignments are gone.
confirmed.symptom: After waking the laptop and pausing at the login screen, previously tiled windows are untiled / missing from their cells; borders blank for those windows.
confirmed.fixDirection: On wake, only resume the validator if the screen is not locked (track lock state from the distributed notifications), or defer resume until screenUnlocked when a lock preceded the sleep.

StateValidator.swift:269-271: 'for (windowID, count) in axOrphanCounts where count >= axOrphanThreshold { await gridState.removeWindowFromAllSpaces(windowID)'. Log shows 0 hits for ws.wake/validate.pause — path untested in production.

confirmed.title: No zero-bounds guard in layout apply: wake/reconnect refresh can tile every window against CGRect.zero
confirmed.mechanism: applyLayoutBody gets display bounds via gridFocus.getDisplayBoundsForSpace (GridApply.swift:136), which resolves to 'display.visibleFrame ?? display.frame ?? .zero' (GridFocus.swift:941) and returns .zero when the space or display is unknown (GridFocus.swift:944,953). The result is fed straight into GridLayout.calculateLayoutWithRatios as screenRect (GridApply.swift:148-150) with no .zero/empty check, and placements are applied via AX (GridApply.swift:383, :476). A nil frame is a real state: DisplayInfoHelper.enrichDisplayInfo returns a DisplayState with nil frame/visibleFrame whenever SLSCopyManagedDisplays lists more displays than NSScreen.screens (DisplayInfo.swift:71-74 'If index is out of bounds, return basic info'), which happens transiently while AppKit lags SkyLight during display negotiation or wake. handleSystemWake Step 2.5 calls gridApply.refreshAllDisplays() at ~t+2.5s after wake (GridReconciler.swift:998), and handleDisplayConnected calls it 500ms after a connect event (GridReconciler.swift:1084-1089) — both squarely inside the negotiation window for USB-C/DisplayLink docks that take 3-10s. Result: cell rects computed from a zero rect, all tiled windows AX-moved to ~(0,0) with degenerate sizes, and persisted there because nothing re-applies later (see displayReconfigured finding).
confirmed.symptom: After sleep/wake or replugging a dock, all tiled windows pile up tiny in the top-left corner of a display and stay there.
confirmed.fixDirection: Guard applyLayoutBody (and refreshAllDisplays per-display) against zero/degenerate displayBounds: log and skip/retry instead of computing placements from CGRect.zero.

confirmed.title: Resolution/scaling/dock changes never reapply layouts: displayReconfigured is UUID-diff-only and ignored by the reconciler
confirmed.mechanism: NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification fires for resolution changes, scaling changes, display rearrangement, and Dock size/visibility changes. WorkspaceObserver routes it as .displayReconfigured(displayUUID: "") (WorkspaceObserver.swift:144-149). StateManager.handleDisplayConfigurationChanged (StateManager.swift:1888) refreshes displays/spaces (so state.displays gets the NEW frames/visibleFrames) but only diffs display UUID SETS (:1903-1905) to decide what to route — a geometry-only change produces empty connected/disconnected sets, so no event reaches the reconciler. GridReconciler's event switch (GridReconciler.swift:446-489) has no .displayReconfigured case at all (falls to 'default: break'). Nothing else reapplies layouts: the displaced-window sweep migrates assignments without repositioning (already-known), and the validator only prunes. So tiled windows keep their pre-change frames forever — overlapping the Dock, hanging off-screen after a resolution drop, or under-filling after an increase — until the user manually runs a layout command. This also blocks recovery from the zero-bounds wake squash: the post-negotiation screen-parameters notification refreshes frames in state but triggers no reapply.
confirmed.symptom: After changing resolution/scaling, moving the Dock, or a display finishing late negotiation, tiled windows are mis-sized/mis-positioned indefinitely (off-screen or overlapping the Dock) until a manual layout command.
confirmed.fixDirection: In handleDisplayConfigurationChanged, diff per-display frame/visibleFrame in addition to UUIDs and route a geometry-changed event; have GridReconciler handle it with refreshAllDisplays (debounced).
confirmed.evidence: WorkspaceObserver.swift:147: 'await EventRouter.shared.route(.displayReconfigured(displayUUID: ""), from: .workspaceObserver)'. StateManager.swift:1903-1905: 'let newDisplayUUIDs = Set(state.displays.map { $0.uuid }); let disconnectedDisplays = oldDisplayUUIDs.subtracting(newDisplayUUIDs); let connectedDisplays = newDisplayUUIDs.subtracting(oldDisplayUUIDs)' — frames never compared. GridReconciler.swift:446-489 switch lists windowCreated/Destroyed/Moved, systemWoke, lock/unlock, displayConnected/Disconnected, appTerminated — no displayReconfigured case; 'default: // Ignore other events'.
