confirmed.title: Wake space-ID migration pairs a stale persisted snapshot positionally (string-sorted) and clobbers destination space state
confirmed.mechanism: handleSystemWake Step 1 builds per-display space lists sorted as STRINGS ('spaceIDs.sorted()' on [String], GridReconciler.swift:974 — so "999" > "1001" lexicographically) and calls gridState.migrateSpaceIDs (GridReconciler.swift:977). migrateSpaceIDs (GridState.swift:236-277) pairs oldSpaceList[i] with newSpaceList[i] positionally (:247-249) where oldSpaceList comes from GridState.displaySpaces (:244). That snapshot has exactly ONE writer: migrateSpaceIDs itself (:270) — confirmed via grep (writers: :119 decode, :169 reset, :270). It is persisted to disk (:119/:149) and is NEVER updated by normal operation: live fullscreen space-ID reassignments go through migrateSpace (GridState.swift:207-233), which rewrites spaces keys but not displaySpaces; the log shows 130 'reconcile.space.reassign' events, so the snapshot is guaranteed stale by the next wake. Consequences: (a) on the first wake after server start displaySpaces is empty -> limit=0 -> reassignments that happened during sleep are silently not migrated, leaving GridState keyed by dead space IDs that pruneDeadSpaces (StateValidator.swift:348-359) then deletes — layouts lost; (b) when old/new lists misalign (space created/destroyed since last wake, or numeric IDs straddling a digit-length boundary under lexicographic sort), :255-258 executes 'spaces[newSpaceID] = oldState' which UNCONDITIONALLY overwrites the destination space's real layout/cells with another space's state — cross-space GridState corruption.
confirmed.symptom: After sleep/wake, spaces swap or lose their layouts and cell assignments: windows tile into another space's layout, or a space's grid config disappears entirely ~30s after wake.
confirmed.fixDirection: Keep displaySpaces updated on every refreshSpaces/migrateSpace (snapshot at sleep time, not last wake), sort numerically, and refuse to overwrite a destination space that already hasSignificantState.

confirmed.title: Reconciler's display-disconnect zombie prune is dead code: spaces are refreshed out of wmState before the event is routed
confirmed.mechanism: StateManager.handleDisplayConfigurationChanged calls refreshDisplays()/refreshSpaces() FIRST (StateManager.swift:1899-1900; refreshSpaces fully replaces state.spaces from SLSCopyManagedDisplaySpaces at :493), and only THEN routes .displayDisconnected (:1922-1927). EventRouter dispatches handlers sequentially (EventRouter.swift:202-214) in registration order — StateManager first (registered in start(), StateManager.swift:120, main.swift:161) so its handleDisplayDisconnected (:1712-1724) refreshes again, then GridReconciler.handleDisplayDisconnected (GridReconciler.swift:1107) fetches wmState (:1115) and computes affectedSpaceIDs = spaces where 'space.displayUUID == displayUUID' (:1118-1120). Since SLS no longer reports the disconnected display (its spaces are gone or re-parented to the surviving display's UUID), affectedSpaceIDs is always empty and the handler early-returns at :1122-1125 logging 'no_spaces'. The entire prune loop (:1130-1139) — the stated purpose of the 'Enhanced disconnect handler' (:1098-1101, 'preventing zombies from accumulating') — can never run. The handler's recovery assumption is also wrong: ':1128-1129 Windows will reappear via windowCreated events when the display reconnects' — existing windows that macOS shoved onto the surviving display emit no windowCreated, so they are never re-tiled there.

confirmed.fixDirection: Capture the disconnected display's space IDs (or pass them in the event payload) BEFORE refreshSpaces rewrites state.spaces, or have the reconciler diff GridState's own per-display space map instead of post-refresh wmState.

confirmed.title: Atomic setCellAssignments path silently drops assignment deltas (no rebuild when cell+focus unchanged)
confirmed.mechanism: GridReconciler.syncBordersForSpace ALWAYS passes focusedWindowID (GridReconciler.swift:1249-1252), so every reconciler border push takes the 'atomic' branch of setCellAssignmentsImpl (SimpleBorderManager.swift:165). That branch only dispatches on three conditions: display/cell changed -> rebuildBorderPool (:178-179), focused window changed -> reassignBorders (:180-184), else -> refreshBorderPositions() (:185-189). The assignments-content comparison `let assignmentsChanged = oldAssignments != assignments` exists ONLY in the non-atomic else-if branch (:201-205), which is unreachable when focusedWindowID is supplied. So when the window membership of the active cell changes while focus and cell stay the same (window sent to the active cell via cell-send, new window auto-assigned to the focused cell, window moved OUT of the active cell to another cell), the manager stores the new assignments dict (:152) but only refreshes positions of EXISTING borders (:691-718). Consequences: (a) split-mode cell: a window newly added to the active cell never gets an inactive border, and a window removed from the active cell keeps its inactive border — handleWindowMovedImpl (:326-334) keeps moving that orphaned border with the window even though it now lives in a different cell; (b) tabbed mode (default): computeStackIndicator (:924-952) is only re-run by applyActiveStyle during rebuild/reassign, so the stack indicator shows a stale window count/index. All of this persists until the next focus or cell change.
confirmed.symptom: Orphaned gray border following a window that was moved to another cell; missing border on a window newly added to the active split cell; stack-indicator tick count wrong (shows N windows when N±1 exist) after sending a window to/from the focused cell without changing focus.
confirmed.fixDirection: In the atomic branch's final else, compare oldAssignments (filtered to the active cell) against the new assignments and call rebuildBorderPool (or targeted acquire/release + applyActiveStyle) when the cell membership changed; otherwise keep refreshBorderPositions.

confirmed.title: @unchecked Sendable violated: bare Task{} logging blocks read freePool/activeBorder/focusedWindowID off the main queue
confirmed.mechanism: The class is declared `@unchecked Sendable` with the invariant 'all mutable state is accessed on DispatchQueue.main' (SimpleBorderManager.swift:26-28). But several methods spawn bare `Task { }` blocks whose closures evaluate the log-data dictionary INSIDE the task. These methods are plain (non-@MainActor) class methods, so `Task {}` inherits no actor isolation and runs on the global concurrent executor — off the main queue. rebuildBorderPool's Task (:676-685) reads `activeBorder`, `focusedWindowID`, `isActiveCellTabbed`, and `freePool.count`; refreshBorderPositions' Task (:712-717) reads `activeCellID`; releaseAllBordersToPool's Task (:816-822) reads `freePool.count`; releaseBorder's evict Task (:787-792) reads `freePool.count` and captures the non-Sendable BorderWindow `oldest` (and reads oldest.windowID AFTER destroy() already zeroed it at BorderWindow.swift:265, so bdr.pool.evict would always log wid:0). Meanwhile the main queue continues mutating freePool via append/popLast/removeFirst on the very next queued operation (1,899 rebuilds + 1,899 releaseAll + 4,591 assignment pushes in the log). Concurrent read of a Swift Array's count during a CoW mutation is a data race / undefined behavior — at minimum the logged values are torn/wrong, at worst a rare crash. Notably the file's own comment (:235-237) calls empty-assignments 'a recurring pre-crash pattern', i.e. the server has crashed in border-adjacent activity.
confirmed.symptom: Rare unexplained server crash during heavy border churn (cell/display switching); incorrect poolSize/focused/tabbed values in bdr.rebuild / bdr.pool.releaseAll log events poisoning post-mortems.
confirmed.fixDirection: Capture all mutable-state values into immutable locals BEFORE spawning the Task (as destroyAllBorders :555-563 already does correctly), or make the class @MainActor and drop @unchecked Sendable.
lenses: round2:Borders subsystem: SimpleBorderManager + BorderWindow (~2,000 untouched LOC, @unchecked Sendable, 1,899 full pool rebuilds in logs)

confirmed.title: BorderWindow.retarget commits targetWindowID before the bounds guard; failure leaves the active border visibly stuck on the old window
confirmed.mechanism: retarget(to:) (BorderWindow.swift:442) assigns `targetWindowID = newTargetID` at :449 BEFORE the SLSGetWindowBounds guard at :453. If bounds for the new target can't be read (window already destroyed — realistic given the known reconciler bugs where destroy events are dropped during suppression, or a focus change racing window close), it logs err.bdr.retarget and returns at :463 WITHOUT repositioning, without moveToTargetSpace, and without hiding. The border stays fully visible at the OLD window's frame with active styling, but its targetWindowID now points at the dead window. The tabbed-mode caller reassignBorders (SimpleBorderManager.swift:583-587) calls `border.retarget(to: newFocused)` and then `applyActiveStyle(to: border)` with no way to detect the failure (retarget returns Void) — applyActiveStyle -> updateBorderStyle (:909-920) then ALSO fails its own SLSGetWindowBounds for the dead target, but still calls border.updateStyle -> show() (:527), re-asserting alpha 1.0. No subsequent handleWindowMoved will arrive for the dead target, so the stale border rectangle persists until the next cell/display change rebuild.
confirmed.symptom: A red/active border rectangle frozen at the previous window's position (possibly over empty desktop after that window closes) while focus has moved elsewhere; clears only on the next cell switch.
confirmed.fixDirection: Make retarget return Bool (or only commit targetWindowID after the bounds guard) and have reassignBorders hide/release the border and acquire a fresh one (or fall back to rebuildBorderPool) on failure.

confirmed.title: queryBorderInfo does DispatchQueue.main.sync from the socket client thread — borders.query RPC hangs if main is wedged
confirmed.mechanism: queryBorderInfo (SimpleBorderManager.swift:479-492) is the only synchronous-blocking entry point in the file: when not on main it does `DispatchQueue.main.sync { ... }` at :486-488. Its sole caller is the borders.query RPC handler (MessageHandler.swift:1323), and MessageHandler.handle runs synchronously on SocketServer's clientQueue (SocketServer.swift:133-134 `clientQueue.async { self?.handleClient(...) }`, :189 `handleRequest(request, ...)` inside the per-client read loop). So the client's entire read loop blocks until the main queue drains. There is no timeout. This is the same blocking-sync-into-main pattern as the already-confirmed StateManager.removeObserver deadlock (StateManager.swift:1222): if the main queue is ever blocked or saturated (e.g., heavy SLS redraw storms from the 1,899 full pool rebuilds, or any future main-blocking bug), the borders.query client hangs indefinitely and that clientQueue thread is consumed. clientQueue is concurrent (:10) so other clients survive, which caps severity at low.
confirmed.symptom: `thegrid` borders.query CLI invocation hangs forever (no response, no error) when the server's main thread is busy/wedged; one leaked client-handler thread per attempt.
confirmed.fixDirection: Convert queryBorderInfo to the same async withCheckedContinuation + main.async bridge used by the BorderRendering conformance (:1092-1165) and make the RPC handler await it inside its Task.
lenses: round2:Borders subsystem: SimpleBorderManager + BorderWindow (~2,000 untouched LOC, @unchecked Sendable, 1,899 full pool rebuilds in logs)

The headline bug holds end-to-end: off-main main.sync with no timeout means borders.query hangs forever if the main queue is wedged, and the BorderRendering async-bridge fix direction (~:1090) is valid. confirmed.title: handleWindowDestroyed prunes cellAssignmentsPerDisplay but not windowOrderPerDisplay — stack indicator counts dead windows
confirmed.mechanism: handleWindowDestroyedImpl (SimpleBorderManager.swift:346-376) removes the dead wid from every display's cellAssignmentsPerDisplay (:373-375, with an explicit 'prevent unbounded growth' comment) but never touches windowOrderPerDisplay, cellStackModesPerDisplay, or displayFramePerDisplay. computeStackIndicator (:924-952) prefers the cached order verbatim: `if let providedOrder = windowOrderPerDisplay[displayUUID]?[cellID] { windowsInCell = providedOrder }` (:934-935), so totalCount includes the destroyed window and currentIndex can be computed against a list containing dead wids. The next applyActiveStyle after a destroy (e.g., focus reassignment to the surviving window in the cell) therefore renders a stack indicator with one tick too many. It self-heals only when the reconciler's next syncBordersForSpace pushes fresh windowOrder (GridReconciler.swift:1254) — and per the known reconciler findings, destroy events dropped during suppression can delay that for many seconds. Cells deleted from layouts also linger in windowOrderPerDisplay forever (the unbounded-growth concern the adjacent code explicitly tried to fix for assignments).
confirmed.symptom: Tabbed-cell stack indicator briefly (or for several seconds under reconciler suppression) shows the wrong tab count / wrong position after closing a window in the active cell.
confirmed.fixDirection: In handleWindowDestroyedImpl, also strip the wid from every windowOrderPerDisplay[*][*] array (mirroring the cellAssignments cleanup loop).

confirmed.title: Picker-launched window claimed during an in-flight applyLayout is silently clobbered by setWindowAssignments
confirmed.mechanism: handle() checks pendingLaunchTarget for windowCreated BEFORE the suppression guard (GridReconciler.swift:421-428: 'Picker-launched windows must be claimed even during move suppression'), so handlePendingLaunchWindow runs while a layout.apply executeAction is suppressing. At GridReconciler.swift:800-804 it does gridState.prependWindow(windowID, toCellID: target.cellID), setFocus, and applyCellLayout. If an applyLayoutBody for the same space is between its assignment read (GridApply.swift:167 getWindowAssignments) and its write (GridApply.swift:266 setWindowAssignments), the new window is in neither the wmState snapshot taken at :135 nor previousAssignments, so assignment.assignments (computed at :171) omits it. setWindowAssignments at :266 then rebuilds space.cells wholesale from that map (GridState.swift:592-636: 'space.cells = [:]' then only cells/windows in the assignments map), erasing the prependWindow claim. The picker window stays AX-positioned in the cell (placed by applyCellLayout at :804) but is absent from GridState — untracked until some later sweep or event re-assigns it, typically by position into whatever cell it overlaps.
confirmed.symptom: App launched via the picker lands in the chosen cell, then on the next layout reapply/focus operation it is treated as unassigned: it gets re-tiled into the wrong cell, loses its slot, or is ignored by focus navigation, especially when the launch coincides with a layout apply / wake refresh / display-connect refresh.
confirmed.fixDirection: Make applyLayoutBody re-read assignments and merge (rather than wholesale replace) at write time, or queue pendingLaunch claims while suppressionDepth > 0 and apply them after the action ends.

confirmed.title: No per-space serialization of applyLayout: concurrent request Tasks interleave cycleLayout state wipes and wholesale assignment writes, producing mixed-layout state
confirmed.mechanism: Every socket request runs in its own unstructured Task (MessageHandler.swift:52 'Task {' inside handle()), clients are handled on a concurrent queue (SocketServer.swift:10 'attributes: .concurrent', :133 clientQueue.async), and GridCommandRouter.dispatch (GridCommandRouter.swift:158-210) has no lock; executeAction (GridReconciler.swift:91-129) only increments suppressionDepth — it provides zero mutual exclusion between two concurrent bodies. So two rapid 'layout cycle' hotkey presses run concurrently: press B executes gridState.cycleLayout (GridCommandRouter.swift:399) -> setCurrentLayout (GridState.swift:285-296) which wipes space.cells, focusedCell, and track ratios WHILE press A's applyLayoutBody is mid-flight; A then writes setWindowAssignments at GridApply.swift:266 with cells computed for layout A into a space whose currentLayoutId is now layout B — cell IDs that may not exist in layout B. Both bodies also race the AX placement phase (:249), so on-screen positions are whichever TaskGroup finished last while GridState reflects the other apply. handleDisplayConnected's refreshAllDisplays (GridReconciler.swift:1089) and command-driven applies are likewise unfenced against each other (only wake refresh is awaited, GridCommandRouter.swift:167).
confirmed.symptom: Hammering the layout-cycle/apply hotkey (or a layout command landing during a display-reconnect refresh) leaves currentLayoutId and the cell map from different layouts: subsequent cell/resize commands error with cellNotFoundInLayout or operate on phantom cells, window positions don't match the reported layout, and a follow-up reapply scrambles assignments.
confirmed.fixDirection: Serialize the apply pipeline per space (actor or AsyncSemaphore keyed by spaceID) around the whole read-compute-write body, and move the cycleLayout/previousLayout state mutation inside that critical section.

SocketServer.swift:10: 'clientQueue = DispatchQueue(label: "com.thegrid.client", attributes: .concurrent)'. GridCommandRouter.swift:399-400: 'let newLayoutID = await gridState.cycleLayout(...); try await gridApply.applyLayout(...)'. GridState.swift:289-293: 'space.cells = [:]; space.focusedCell = ""; ... space.columnRatios = nil'. GridReconciler.swift:99: 'suppressionDepth += 1' (no exclusion). GridApply.swift:167/266 read-then-replace of assignments. Logs show applies completing within the same second (e.g. two layout.apply.start/done pairs at ts 1781143692), so sub-second key repeats overlap.

confirmed.title: resize grow/shrink is inverted when the focused window is the last in its cell stack
confirmed.mechanism: adjustFocusedSplit picks the boundary as boundaryIndex = focused index, but when the focused window is the last in the stack it falls back to the previous boundary (GridResize.swift:93-96: 'var boundaryIndex = idx; if boundaryIndex >= ratios.count - 1 { boundaryIndex = ratios.count - 2 }') WITHOUT negating delta. adjustSplitRatio (GridLayout.swift:687-718) does newFirst = ratios[index] + delta; newSecond = ratios[index+1] - delta. For focused idx < last, ratios[idx] grows — correct. For focused idx == last, ratios[count-2] (the NEIGHBOR) grows by delta and ratios[count-1] (the focused window) SHRINKS by delta — 'resize grow' shrinks the focused window and 'resize shrink' grows it. The cell-boundary variant handles this correctly via 'let adjustDelta = isGrowing ? delta : -delta' (GridResize.swift:240); the split variant lacks the equivalent negation. Trigger is common: GridState.assignWindow appends new windows at the END of cell.windows and focuses them (GridState.swift:336-338), so the last window is frequently the focused one.
confirmed.symptom: With the bottom/right-most (or any last-in-stack, e.g. newly opened) window focused, the grow hotkey makes it smaller and shrink makes it bigger — inverted resize behavior. resize.split.done logged 63 times, so this path is heavily used.
confirmed.fixDirection: When clamping boundaryIndex to ratios.count - 2 for the last window, negate delta (or call adjustSplitRatio with index = idx-1 and delta = -delta).
confirmed.evidence: GridResize.swift:93-104: 'var boundaryIndex = idx; if boundaryIndex >= ratios.count - 1 { boundaryIndex = ratios.count - 2 } ... GridLayout.adjustSplitRatio(ratios: ratios, index: boundaryIndex, delta: delta, ...)'. GridLayout.swift:702-703: 'var newFirst = newRatios[index] + delta; var newSecond = newRatios[index + 1] - delta'. Contrast GridResize.swift:240: 'let adjustDelta = isGrowing ? delta : -delta'. Logs: 63x '"ev":"resize.split.done"'.

confirmed.mechanism: handleLayout 'cycle' calls gridState.cycleLayout (GridCommandRouter.swift:399) which immediately commits setCurrentLayout (GridState.swift:285-296), wiping space.cells, focusedCell, focusedWindow and track ratios, BEFORE applyLayout is invoked at :400 (same for 'previous' at :409-410). If applyLayout then throws — gridConfig.getLayout at GridApply.swift:132 (config reloaded/renamed between getLayoutIDs and getLayout), the guard-let at GridApply.swift:81-86, or any future throw in the body — the catch at GridCommandRouter.swift:206-208 just returns an error: the previous layout's assignments are already destroyed and never restored, and currentLayoutId/layoutIndex already point at the new layout. Even on success, the wipe happens outside any suppression window (executeAction begins only inside applyLayout at GridApply.swift:94), so a reconcile/focus sweep firing between :399 and :400 observes a space with zero cells.
confirmed.symptom: A failed layout cycle (e.g. config edited concurrently) leaves every window on the space untiled and focus state empty; user must manually reapply a layout. Transient empty-cell window also lets a sweep mis-handle windows as unassigned.
confirmed.fixDirection: Move the cycleLayout/setCurrentLayout mutation inside applyLayoutBody (it already calls setCurrentLayout at GridApply.swift:263) and pass only the computed target layout ID from the router; never pre-commit the wipe.

confirmed.title: assignWindow/removeWindow equalize splitRatios on every membership change while setWindowAssignments preserves them — cell send wipes custom splits in both cells
confirmed.mechanism: GridCellOps.sendWindow moves a window via gridState.removeWindow + gridState.assignWindow (GridCellOps.swift:118-119). removeWindow resets the source cell's ratios to equal (GridState.swift:415-419: 'cell.splitRatios = equalRatios(cell.windows.count)') and assignWindow resets the target cell's ratios to equal (GridState.swift:339). The reapplyLayout that follows (GridCellOps.swift:127) reads those now-equalized ratios at GridApply.swift:205 and places windows accordingly. This contradicts the preservation logic in setWindowAssignments (GridState.swift:618-623), which deliberately carries old ratios through count changes via adjustRatiosForCount, and in applyLayoutBody step 8 (GridApply.swift:209-211) which adjusts rather than resets. So the apply pipeline tries to preserve user split adjustments, but the cell-send/event-assignment path (also handleWindowCreated -> assignWindow) destroys them first.
confirmed.symptom: Carefully adjusted split ratios in a cell snap back to equal whenever any window is sent into or out of that cell, or when a new window opens and is auto-assigned to it — while a plain layout reapply preserves them, making the behavior feel random.
confirmed.fixDirection: In assignWindow/removeWindow, use recalculateSplitsAfterAddition/recalculateSplitsAfterRemoval (already implemented in GridLayout.swift:781-825 and currently dead for this path) instead of equalRatios.
confirmed.evidence: GridState.swift:339: 'cell.splitRatios = equalRatios(cell.windows.count)' (assignWindow), GridState.swift:418 same in removeWindow; versus GridState.swift:619-622: 'if existingCell.splitRatios.count == windowIDs.count { cell.splitRatios = existingCell.splitRatios } else { cell.splitRatios = adjustRatiosForCount(...) }'. GridCellOps.swift:118-119 invokes the resetting pair on every cell send.

suspected.title: deriveSpaceFromDisplay rewrites window.spaces to the display's CURRENT space, overriding SLS truth for windows on inactive spaces
suspected.mechanism: deriveSpaceFromDisplay (StateManager.swift:945-982) sets 'window.spaces = [display.currentSpaceID]' for ANY non-sticky window whose geometric center lands on a display (:952-955), discarding the SLSCopySpacesForWindows result that refreshWindows correctly fetched (StateManager.swift:1114-1132, overridden at 1135-1137). It re-runs on every poll (updateWindowFromPoll :1369-1372), every AX move/resize (:1561-1585), and at window add (:1436-1439, :1498-1501). Windows on an INACTIVE space of a display keep valid frames in CGWindowList, so after a space switch every tracked window on the old space gets spaces rewritten to the NEW space within one 3s poll. GridReconciler.sweepDisplacedWindows (GridReconciler.swift:1394-1446), run at every action exit, then sees tracked=oldSpace vs actual=[newSpace], resolveDisplacedTarget (:1339-1359) returns newSpace, and the window is removed from its real space and dumped into the focused cell of the new space (:1423-1426). The same derivation feeds resolveWindowSpace at window creation (:1294-1307), explaining the observed pattern of freshly created Simulator windows assigned to space 6 then lift.migrate'd to space 3 minutes later.
suspected.symptom: On any multi-space-per-display workflow, switching spaces then pressing any hotkey strips the previous space's tiling assignments and piles those windows into one cell of the new space; new windows can be assigned to a cell on the wrong space/display and later get bounced by the displacement sweep.
suspected.fixDirection: Only derive space from display when SLS returns empty/failed, or restrict the geometric override to windows currently on-screen (isHidden == false); never overwrite a non-empty SLS space list for an off-screen window.
suspected.evidence: StateManager.swift:952-955: 'if let displayUUID = window.displayUUID, let display = state.displays.first(...), display.currentSpaceID != 0 { window.spaces = [display.currentSpaceID] }' — unconditional for non-sticky windows. Logs: {"ev":"reconcile.lift.migrate","data":{"cell":"right","from":"6","to":"3","wid":5760},"ts":1780806467} fired for 5 freshly-created windows (5032, 5433, 5735, 5760, 5771) whose tracked space disagreed with derived OS space minutes after creation, with zero reconcile.space.change events in the entire log.

CONFIRMED hops: (1) deriveSpaceFromDisplay (StateManager.swift:945-983) unconditionally sets window.spaces=[display.currentSpaceID] at :952-955 for any non-sticky window with a geometric display hit; originalSpaces (the SLS truth fetched at :1114-1132) is used only as fallback, and there is no isHidden/on-screen guard (only isMinimized in computeDisplayUUID :935-940). (4) GridReconciler hops exist as cited: resolveWindowSpace :1294-1307, resolveDisplacedTarget :1339-1359, sweepDisplacedWindows :1394-1446 dumping into the focused cell :1423-1426, run at every suppression-depth-0 exit (:109-110, :121-122, :152-154). suspected.title: restoreFocusForSpace can AX-raise a window that moved to another space, yanking the user off the space they just switched to
suspected.mechanism: On space switch, StateManager.handleSpaceChanged calls restoreFocusForSpace(newSpaceID) (StateManager.swift:1794-1796). restoreFocusForSpace (:1830-1860) takes space.lastFocusedWindowID and issues manipulator.focusWindow (:1852-1853) after checking only that the window exists in state and is not hidden/minimized (:1838-1841). It never checks window.spaces still contains spaceID. lastFocusedWindowID is written only at focus time (:746, :819, :825) and is never invalidated when the window is later moved to a different space. focusWindowWithRaise (WindowManipulator.swift:458-482) raises via SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions + AXRaise, which makes macOS switch to the window's current space — so switching to space A immediately bounces the user to space B. The raise is also issued with no reconciler fence/suppression, so the resulting focus events are processed as organic. Dormant in the current log (0 win.focus.restore hits), so confidence is suspected for the end-to-end trigger, but every code hop is real.
suspected.symptom: Switching to a space immediately bounces you to a different space (where a previously-focused window now lives), or focuses a window the user did not expect.
suspected.fixDirection: Verify window.spaces.contains(spaceID) (and tileability) before restoring, and clear/refresh space.lastFocusedWindowID when a window's space assignment changes.
suspected.evidence: StateManager.swift:1838-1841 'guard let window = state.windows[String(windowID)], !window.isHidden && !window.isMinimized else { return }' — no space membership check; :1852-1853 'let manipulator = WindowManipulator(connectionID: connectionID); let success = manipulator.focusWindow(pid: window.pid, windowID: windowID)'. Log: grep -c '"ev":"win.focus.restore"' = 0 (path dormant or silently bailing).

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-read every cited hop and all of them hold in code: (1) StateManager.swift:1794-1796 calls restoreFocusForSpace(newSpaceID) from handleSpaceChanged whenever a display's currentSpaceID changed (:1742-1751), wired from NSWorkspace activeSpaceDidChange via WorkspaceObserver.swift:132-142 → StateManager.swift:232-233. (2) restoreFocusForSpace (:1830-1860) guards only on space entry + lastFocusedWindowID non-nil (:1832-1834) and window-exists + !isHidden + !isMinimized (:1838-1841) — no window.spaces.contains(spaceID) check, even though window.spaces is freshly re-queried at :1781-1787 immediately before. (3) grep over GridServer confirms lastFocusedWindowID is written only at :746 (updateActiveSpace via applyWindowFocus/handleWindowFocused), :819/:825 (setFocusedWindow), preserved at :469-472, and is never cleared when a window's space assignment changes (handleWindowSpaceAssignmentChanged does not touch it). (4) focusWindow → focusWindowWithRaise (WindowManipulator.swift:501-509, 458-482) issues SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions + synthesized key events + AXRaise. (5) No suppression: restoreFocusForSpace never calls markCLIFocusIntent (:790), so resulting focus events are organic. Git history: restoreFocusForSpace dates to early commit af58c8d and is unchanged through recent commits; working tree has no StateManager.swift modifications. The verdict stays 'suspected' rather than 'confirmed' because two hops cannot be verified end-to-end: (a) the claim that the raise makes macOS switch to the window's current space is platform behavior with no in-repo proof (theGrid's own space.focus uses a separate mss_space_focus path, MSSClient.swift:449); (b) log forensics show the trigger has never fired — 0 win.focus.restore across 122 spc.changed events — and I traced why: every spc.changed in the log is a space-ID reassignment (3→419→3 etc.), and refreshSpaces wholesale-replaces state.spaces (:493) while the preserve at :469-472 keys on the new sid, wiping lastFocusedWindowID each time, so the first guard always bails on this machine (only one user space per display here). The mechanism is real code-wise and would be exercised on a setup with multiple stable user spaces per display, but the end-to-end yank could not be demonstrated.

Paired with StateManager.swift:493 (state.spaces = spaces, wholesale replace) and :469-472 (preserve keyed on the NEW spaceID, which has no prior entry after a renumber), lastFocusedWindowID is wiped on every reassignment — this concretely explains the 0 win.focus.restore hits the finder flagged as 'dormant or silently bailing': the first guard (:1832-1834) bails every time on this machine. Also: deployed binary contains the 'win.focus.restore' string (strings grep = 1), so the path exists in the running build; win.focus events write sid 3/6 constantly (last 200: {6:106, 3:94}), confirming the write path at :746 is live. Additional unsuppressed-raise evidence: restoreFocusForSpace issues manipulator.focusWindow without calling markCLIFocusIntent (:790), unlike CLI focus paths, so any resulting AX focus cascade is treated as organic.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code re-read confirms every hop: restoreFocusForSpace (grid-server/Sources/GridServer/StateManager.swift:1830-1860) guards only on space existence + lastFocusedWindowID (:1832-1835) and window existence/!isHidden/!isMinimized (:1838-1841) — no window.spaces.contains(spaceID) check — then calls manipulator.focusWindow (:1852-1853); focusWindowWithRaise (WindowManipulator.swift:457-482) does SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions + makeKeyWindow + AXRaise, which would indeed follow the window to its current space. suspected.title: Poll snapshot TOCTOU resurrects destroyed windows and routes phantom windowCreated events
suspected.mechanism: The 3s poll timer captures CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo OFF the actor (StateManager.swift:1240-1245), then hops onto the actor via Task { await self?.applyPollResults(windowList) } (:1246-1248). Between snapshot and apply, an AX windowDestroyed can be processed (handleWindowDestroyed, :1525, removes the window from state.windows). applyPollResults then finds the stale wid in the snapshot, the lookup 'state.windows[String(windowID)]' at :1272 returns nil, so the dead window is treated as 'New window discovered by poll' (:1278-1286): addWindowFromPoll re-inserts it and a fire-and-forget Task routes .windowCreated(from: .poll) (:1291-1300). GridReconciler.handleWindowCreated then sees it in wmState (just re-added) and can assign it to a cell (GridReconciler.swift:687-694). The ghost is removed only on the NEXT poll tick (absent from the fresh CGWindowList, :1303-1331) or by the validator — up to 3s of ghost state plus a spurious create/destroy pair sent to the reconciler.
suspected.symptom: Closed window briefly reappears in grid state and cell assignments; back-to-back ev.win.create(src=poll) then ev.win.destroy(src=poll) for the same wid ~3s apart; transient wrong window counts in cells.
suspected.fixDirection: Keep a short-lived tombstone set of recently destroyed wids (with destroy timestamp) and skip poll re-adds whose snapshot predates the destroy.

suspected.title: AX properties are only re-queried while role is nil — window misclassified at creation (e.g. transient AXUnknown subrole) stays rejected forever
suspected.mechanism: updateWindowFromPoll re-queries getAXProperties only under 'if window.role == nil' (StateManager.swift:1355-1367); refreshAXPropertiesForActiveSpace has the same guard (:992). A window that returned role="AXWindow" but a transient subrole ("AXUnknown" during app startup) at creation time keeps that cached subrole permanently. Downstream, isTileable rejects any non-empty subrole != "AXStandardWindow" (GridAssignment.swift:121-123), so the reconciler rejects it (GridReconciler.swift:588-598 -> gridState.rejectWindow). The rescue paths cannot help: rejectedWindowSweep re-checks isTileable against the same stale cached WindowState (GridReconciler.swift:394-395), and handleWindowMoved does the same cached check (:1036). Only a duplicate AXCreated notification (re-running StateManager.handleWindowCreated:1446) can refresh the subrole — apps that emit exactly one AXCreated never recover. Logs show real-sized windows rejected on AXUnknown: wid 8582 (912x416) at ts 1781189913; whether any was a long-lived window the user wanted tiled is not provable from this log (8582 was destroyed 2s later), hence suspected.

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every hop. Code mechanism holds end-to-end: StateManager.swift:1355 guards AX re-query on `window.role == nil` exactly as claimed; refreshAXPropertiesForActiveSpace:992 has the same guard; all five `subrole =` write sites were enumerated (:1001, :1087, :1359, :1423, :1485) and none refreshes subrole for an existing role!=nil window during normal operation; isTileable (GridAssignment.swift:121-123) permanently rejects subrole "AXUnknown"; GridReconciler.swift:588-598 rejects, and both rescue paths (rejectedWindowSweep :394-395, handleWindowMoved :1030-1036) re-check isTileable against the cached WindowState from stateProvider.getState(), which returns cached state with no AX re-query (StateManager.swift:137-139). However the trigger premise — that macOS reports a transient AXUnknown subrole that later resolves to AXStandardWindow on a window the user wants tiled — could not be verified and is actively weakened by log mining: of 374 AXUnknown-rejected windows in ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json, zero ever appeared later with AXStandardWindow, and every long-lived one was a 0x0 phantom or a 1441x88 toolbar that fails isTileable on dimensions regardless of subrole (e.g. wid 6436/6451/7104 role=nil 0x0; wid 3879 1441x88). Additionally GridReconciler.swift:1033-1035 comments show the isTileable re-check in handleWindowMoved was deliberately added to prevent unrejecting "Chrome AXUnknown dropdowns", i.e. the developers treat AXUnknown as a stable classification. Not refuted (the staleness is real code behavior and would fire if a transient subrole ever occurs), not confirmed (hop 7, the transient-subrole trigger, unverified and the claimed symptom has no observed victim in the logs).

suspected.title: Display-reconnect reapply runs against a state snapshot taken before macOS finishes migrating spaces back
suspected.mechanism: On reconnect, StateManager.handleDisplayConfigurationChanged refreshes state and routes .displayConnected; StateManager.handleDisplayConnected (StateManager.swift:1705-1709) refreshes again, THEN GridReconciler.handleDisplayConnected sleeps 500ms 'to let macOS stabilize' (GridReconciler.swift:1084) and calls gridApply.refreshAllDisplays(displayFilter:) (:1089). But nothing re-refreshes StateManager's cached state AFTER the 500ms: refreshAllDisplays reads stateProvider.getState() (GridApply.swift:402) which returns the snapshot built before the sleep, and findSpaceIDForDisplay uses display.currentSpaceID captured at that pre-sleep refreshDisplays (GridApply.swift:567-569). If macOS migrates the display's spaces back from the laptop screen during/after the 500ms window (typical: space re-parenting completes seconds after the display appears), the reapply targets a stale or wrong space ID, or errors with noDisplayBounds. Later didChangeScreenParametersNotification firings refresh state but produce no UUID diff, so no second reapply ever happens (see displayReconfigured finding) — windows that were shoved to the laptop screen are never repositioned onto the re-plugged display.
suspected.symptom: After replugging an external display, its windows stay on the laptop screen / are not snapped back into their cells; layout refresh appears to run but does nothing for the reconnected display.
suspected.fixDirection: Re-trigger a StateManager refresh (displays + spaces) after the 500ms settle delay and before refreshAllDisplays, or retry the reapply when a later reconfiguration notification shows the display's currentSpaceID changed.
suspected.evidence: GridReconciler.swift:1081-1089: '// Short delay allows macOS to stabilize space/window state after reconnect... try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(500)); let errors = await gridApply?.refreshAllDisplays(displayFilter: displayUUID)'. GridApply.swift:402: 'let wmState = await stateProvider.getState()' (cached state, no SLS re-query). GridApply.swift:567-569: 'if let display = wmState.displays.first(where: { $0.uuid == displayUUID }), display.currentSpaceID != 0 { return String(display.currentSpaceID) }'. StateManager handler runs before reconciler (EventRouter.swift:202-214 sequential; StateManager registers first at StateManager.swift:120).
suspected.logSignature: "ev":"warn.reconcile.display.connect.errors" or "ev":"layout.refresh_all.done" with processed:1 immediately after "ev":"reconcile.display.connect" while window frames remain on the other display
lenses: round2:Display connect/disconnect/reconfigure + sleep-wake state migration (StateManager 1705-2110, WorkspaceObserver, DisplayInfo, StateValidator pause/resume)

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-traced every cited hop and all code claims hold: (1) WorkspaceObserver.swift:93 wires didChangeScreenParametersNotification -> .displayReconfigured -> StateManager.handleDisplayConfigurationChanged (StateManager.swift:260-261, 1888-1932), which refreshes displays/spaces (1899-1900) and routes .displayConnected ONLY for newly-appearing UUIDs (1903-1920). (2) EventRouter.swift:202-214 dispatches sequentially in registration order; StateManager registers first (StateManager.swift:120, inside start() which completes before gridReconciler.setup() registers at GridReconciler.swift:305 per main.swift:161-166), so StateManager.handleDisplayConnected (StateManager.swift:1705-1709) refreshes before the reconciler runs. (3) GridReconciler.handleDisplayConnected sleeps 500ms (GridReconciler.swift:1084) then calls refreshAllDisplays(displayFilter:) (1089); nothing re-refreshes StateManager state after the sleep — getState() is a plain cached return with no SLS re-query (StateManager.swift:137-139), read at GridApply.swift:402, and findSpaceIDForDisplay keys off cached display.currentSpaceID (GridApply.swift:567-569) or errors noDisplayBounds (414-420, 455-461). (4) The no-recovery claim is fully confirmed: a later displayReconfigured with unchanged UUIDs routes no displayConnected; spaceIDReassigned only migrates GridState + syncs borders, no repositioning (GridReconciler.swift:914-944); spaceCreated/Destroyed hit the reconciler's default:break (446-489); StateValidator only removes assignments (StateValidator.swift:220/270/336); the only other refreshAllDisplays callers are server start (main.swift:241), wake (GridReconciler.swift:998), and manual CLI refresh (GridCommandRouter.swift:416). Git log shows no change to this path since the finding (713cf7a latest). Why not confirmed: the triggering hop — macOS completing space re-parenting more than 500ms after the displayConnected event — is an OS-timing premise unverifiable from code, and I found zero dsp.connected/reconcile.display.connect events in ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json to evidence a real occurrence. Minor wording correction: getState() runs after the sleep and returns live state at that moment (actor reentrancy could let a notification inside the 500ms refresh it), so it is not literally a pre-sleep snapshot — but nothing guarantees a refresh, which is the substantive defect.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: GridReconciler.swift:1107-1129 — handleDisplayDisconnected eagerly removes ALL window assignments for the disconnected display's spaces, with a comment asserting windows "will reappear via windowCreated events when the display reconnects". Already-running windows fire no windowCreated on reconnect, so even a perfectly-timed reapply with .preserve strategy may find empty assignments to restore — an independent mechanism producing the same symptom (windows stranded on the laptop screen) that makes the user-visible failure more likely than the race alone. Also confirmed handleSpaceIDReassigned (GridReconciler.swift:914-944) is migrate+border-sync only — no repositioning — closing the last plausible recovery path.

evidenceVerdict.reasoning: Code evidence actively demonstrates the mechanism. (1) GridReconciler.swift:1077-1095: handleDisplayConnected sleeps 500ms with a comment saying the delay lets macOS stabilize 'before we query it', then calls gridApply.refreshAllDisplays(displayFilter:) — but no query happens after the sleep: GridApply.swift:402 reads stateProvider.getState(), and StateManager.swift:137-139 shows getState() is a pure cached read ('return state'), no SLS re-query. (2) The only refresh (StateManager.swift:1704-1709 handleDisplayConnected → refreshDisplays()/refreshSpaces()) provably runs BEFORE the sleep: EventRouter.swift:202-214 dispatches sequentially in registration order and StateManager registers first (StateManager.swift:120, before GridReconciler is created at main.swift:157 / registers at GridReconciler.swift:305). (3) Space targeting uses the stale field exactly as claimed: GridApply.swift:567-575 findSpaceIDForDisplay reads display.currentSpaceID from the frozen snapshot. The comment/behavior contradiction (sleep exists to let state settle, yet the state read is frozen pre-sleep) confirms the defect structurally. Log side: greps of ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-server.json (153,697 lines, 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-11) found ZERO hits for reconcile.display.connect, warn.reconcile.display.connect.errors, dsp.connected, dsp.disconnected, and dbg.dsp.reconfig.start (the entry point in StateManager.handleDisplayConfigurationChanged, StateManager.swift:1888-1932). Build mismatch ruled out: strings on the deployed binary at ~/.local/state/thegrid/GridServer.app/Contents/MacOS/grid-server contains all these event strings. The 881 'dsp.change' events are innocent (active-display focus tracking at StateManager.swift:711, unrelated to reconfiguration). So the display connect/disconnect path has never executed on this machine in the logged period — the latent bug is real in code but has zero observed real-world frequency here, arguing for a severity downgrade (medium → low) on impact grounds.
evidenceVerdict.addedEvidence: StateManager.swift:137-139: 'func getState() -> WindowManagerState { return state }' — pure cached read, confirming refreshAllDisplays after the 500ms sleep sees only the pre-sleep snapshot. Log absence: 0/153,697 lines contain reconcile.display.connect, dsp.connected, dsp.disconnected, or dbg.dsp.reconfig.start over 10 days (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-11), while the deployed binary verifiably contains those strings — the display-reconnect path has never executed on this machine, so the symptom is unobservable in these logs. Also notable: handleDisplayConfigurationChanged (StateManager.swift:1888) is driven by NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification (WorkspaceObserver.swift:93), and its dbg.dsp.reconfig.start log never appears — the notification itself never fired in 10 days, consistent with a single-display/no-replug setup (or a delivery issue belonging to the separate displayReconfigured finding).

suspected.title: refreshDisplays joins SLS display order to NSScreen.screens by array index — frames/scale can attach to the wrong display UUID
suspected.mechanism: refreshDisplays enumerates SLSCopyManagedDisplays output and passes the loop index as screenIndex (StateManager.swift:404-413) to DisplayInfoHelper.enrichDisplayInfo, which does 'let screen = screens[screenIndex]' over NSScreen.screens (DisplayInfo.swift:70-75). The two arrays come from independent subsystems (SkyLight managed-display order vs AppKit screen order, where only screens[0]=primary is documented); nothing matches the SLS UUID to the NSScreen via CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID. With 2+ displays, any ordering divergence attaches frame/visibleFrame/backingScaleFactor/name of monitor A to the DisplayState of monitor B. Every layout apply consumes these cached frames (GridFocus.swift:941 'display.visibleFrame ?? display.frame ?? .zero' via GridApply.swift:136), so a mismatch tiles windows with the wrong monitor's geometry. Additionally, when SLS reports more displays than AppKit (mid-transition), the out-of-bounds guard returns a DisplayState with nil frame (DisplayInfo.swift:71-74), feeding the unguarded .zero path in layout apply. User runs multi-display (881 dsp.change events), so exposure is real; whether SLS/AppKit orders actually diverge on this machine is unverified, hence suspected.
suspected.symptom: Tiled windows on one monitor sized/positioned as if for the other monitor (wrong resolution/menu-bar inset), especially with 2+ externals or right after arrangement changes.
suspected.fixDirection: Match displays by UUID: map each SLS UUID to the NSScreen whose CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID(screen.displayID) equals it, instead of joining by index.
suspected.evidence:
StateManager.swift:404-411: 'for (index, displayUUID) in displayUUIDs.enumerated() { ... DisplayInfoHelper.enrichDisplayInfo(uuid: displayUUID, screenIndex: index, ...)'. DisplayInfo.swift:69-75: '// Get NSScreen by index (following AeroSpace pattern)
 let screens = NSScreen.screens
 guard screenIndex >= 0 && screenIndex < screens.count else { return display }
 let screen = screens[screenIndex]'.
suspected.logSignature: "ev":"dsp.refresh" followed by placements landing on the wrong display; no dedicated signature exists today (gap)
lenses: round2:Display connect/disconnect/reconfigure + sleep-wake state migration (StateManager 1705-2110, WorkspaceObserver, DisplayInfo, StateValidator pause/resume)

codeVerdict.reasoning: Re-read every cited hop at HEAD: StateManager.swift:404-413 passes the SLSCopyManagedDisplays loop index as screenIndex; DisplayInfo.swift:70-75 indexes NSScreen.screens with it and returns a nil-frame DisplayState when out of bounds; GridFocus.swift:939-944 returns visibleFrame ?? frame ?? .zero by UUID lookup; GridApply.swift:135-150 feeds that unguarded into calculateLayoutWithRatios. Grepped the entire grid-server/Sources for CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID / CFUUIDCreateString — zero hits, so no UUID-based correction exists anywhere. Checked git log -8 for StateManager.swift — no commit changed this mechanism; cited lines match exactly. Hunted refutation angles: no guard prevents the join (the only guard, DisplayInfo.swift:71, returns a frameless display — worse); actor isolation is irrelevant because the bug is a cross-API ordering assumption, not a thread race; no debounce — handleDisplayConnected/Disconnected (StateManager.swift:1705-1724) and :1899 call refreshDisplays() synchronously on the SLS-side event, exactly when NSScreen.screens may lag, making the SLS-count > AppKit-count nil-frame window structurally real. The one hop that cannot be verified from code: whether SLS and AppKit orderings actually diverge on this machine (both commonly list primary first; SLS has no documented order contract). All code hops hold; that empirical precondition keeps this 'suspected' rather than 'confirmed'.
codeVerdict.addedEvidence: 1) No UUID matching anywhere: grep for CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID and CFUUIDCreateString across grid-server/Sources returns zero hits. 2) The mid-transition path is structurally concrete: handleDisplayConnected (StateManager.swift:1705-1710) and handleDisplayDisconnected (:1712-1724) fire from SLS notifications and immediately call refreshDisplays(), which reads NSScreen.screens — if AppKit hasn't processed the reconfiguration yet, SLS reports more displays than AppKit and DisplayInfo.swift:71-74 emits nil-frame DisplayStates. 3) The unguarded .zero consumption is wider than cited: besides GridFocus.swift:941 → GridApply.swift:136-150 (no .zero check before calculateLayoutWithRatios), the same 'visibleFrame ?? frame ?? .zero' pattern exists at GridWindowMove.swift:413 and :711 and GridRecorder.swift:133 and :512.

However, real-world evidence does not show the bug firing: (1) I probed both subsystems live (swift scripts calling SLSCopyManagedDisplays via dlsym and CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID per NSScreen) — SLS order [FCEC43D7, 89ED320F] matches NSScreen.screens order exactly on this machine. (2) The server's cached DisplayState (via display_list) matches per-UUID ground truth byte-for-byte: FCEC43D7 frame y=0/scale 2, 89ED320F frame y=-1080/scale 1 — the startup join attached the right attributes to the right UUIDs. The apparent isMain inversion (server says 89ED320F isMain, NSScreen now says FCEC43D7) is innocent: NSScreen.main is the key-window screen, which drifts after startup; not the claimed mechanism. (3) Absence evidence: in 153,701 log lines over 10 days, refreshDisplays ran exactly once (startup, rotated out) — zero dsp.refresh, dsp.connected/disconnected, dbg.dsp.reconfig, warn.dsp, or warn.dsp.cgbounds_empty events. The finding's '881 dsp.change events' are per-window display-change routing (StateManager.swift:711), not display reconfiguration, so they never exercise this path. The mid-transition out-of-bounds/nil-frame branch never fired either. Verdict: the latent defect is real in code but no log or live evidence shows orders diverging on this machine, and the trigger window (display reconfiguration) essentially never opens here — suspected, with severity downgraded for this user's static dual-monitor setup.

Ground truth CGDisplayBounds: FCEC43D7=(0,0,3840,1080) scale 2.0; 89ED320F=(0,-1080,3840,1080) scale 1.0 — identical to server display_list state, proving the startup index-join landed correctly. refuted.title: ax_orphan prune evicts live panel-style windows (hit the GridNotify panel, emptying the 'notify' cell)
refuted.reason: Re-read grid-server/Sources/GridServer/Grid/StateValidator.swift in full — the cited code at :233-277, :282-307, :252, :97, :61, :81 all match the finding's quotes, and git log shows no recent change to the prune logic. But the claimed MECHANISM is wrong. (1) The GridNotify panel is not an NSPanel/nonactivating panel: grid-notify/Sources/GridNotify/NotificationPanelWindow.swift:9 declares `class NotificationPanelWindow: NSWindow` with styleMask [.titled, .closable, .resizable, .fullSizeContentView] (:39), deliberately built to appear as a real window; the server's own win.created log for wid 2858 shows role:AXWindow subrole:AXStandardWindow. (2) The window was not 'alive on screen and AX-invisible' — it was hidden by the user. ~/.local/state/thegrid/thegrid-notify.json shows notify.toggle.hide at ts 1780439954 (grid-notify AppDelegate.swift:127 calls window.orderOut(nil)), the ax_orphan prune at ts 1780439987 (33s later, spanning 2 validator cycles), and notify.toggle.show at ts 1780439994 — which is the supposed 'immediate re-creation'. An ordered-out NSWindow is legitimately absent from kAXWindowsAttribute; that is standard AX behavior, not a panel quirk. The symptom claim 'the window itself stays on screen unmanaged' is directly contradicted. (3) The downstream causality is also wrong: the ax.fail reason:not_in_list focus failures at ts 1780439986 precede the prune at 987, so directional focus into the cell was already failing because the window was hidden, not because it was pruned. (4) 'Routinely': the entire server log (153,053 lines covering 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-11) contains exactly ONE ax_orphan prune — this one — and it self-healed in 7s when the panel was re-shown (reconcile re-placed it into the locked 'notify' cell). The cleared 17/17 resetOrphanCounts events are the space-reassign mitigation (GridReconciler.swift:926) firing as designed during space transitions, not near-misses of this mechanism. (5) The proposed fix (require SLSGetWindowBounds to fail) would be counterproductive: SLS bounds succeed for ordered-out windows (which is why pruneDeadWindows at StateValidator.swift:202-224 didn't prune it as 'dead' in the same cycle), so the fix would pin unfocusable hidden windows in cells forever. Pruning an AX-inaccessible window matches the validator's documented purpose (StateValidator.swift:226-229). At most there is a minor design question — whether ordered-out windows should be skipped like minimized ones (:242) — but the finding's mechanism (live on-screen panels invisible to AX being wrongly evicted) did not occur.
